Certifications: AWS Certified Solutions Architect, Microsoft Certified Azure Solutions Architect Expert, Google Cloud
Professional Cloud Architect, Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)
2. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning:

Job Roles: Data Scientist, AI Engineer, Machine Learning Engineer, NLP Specialist, Deep Learning Engineer
Skills: Python, R, Java; ML frameworks (TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch); Data visualization (Matplotlib, Seaborn); AI/ML
algorithms and statistical models
Certifications: Microsoft Certified Azure AI Engineer Associate, Google Professional Machine Learning Engineer, IBM AI
Engineering Professional Certificate, AWS Certified Machine Learning – Specialty
3. Cyber Security:
Job Roles: Security Analyst, Ethical Hacker (Penetration Tester), Security Architect, SOC Analyst, Cybersecurity Consultant
Skills: Risk management, Ethical hacking tools (Metasploit, Burp Suite), Firewalls, SIEM tools (Splunk, LogRhythm), Incident
response and forensics
Certifications: CEH, CISSP, CISM, CompTIA Security+, CISA
4. Blockchain and Fintech:
Job Roles: Blockchain Developer, Smart Contract Developer, Blockchain Architect, Cryptocurrency Expert, Blockchain Security
Engineer
Skills: Blockchain platforms (Ethereum, Hyperledger, Solana), Smart contract development (Solidity, Rust), DApp development
Certifications: Certified Blockchain Developer, Ethereum Developer Certification, Certified Blockchain Professional (CBCP)

Job Roles: Network Administrator, IT Systems Engineer, IT Infrastructure Manager, Virtualization Engineer, Network Security
Engineer

Certifications: CCNA, CompTIA Network+, CISA, VMware Certified Professional (VCP)

MSAJCE library institutional memberships (DELNET and J-Gate), and the complete set of library rules, regulations, and fine structure for

Institution Membership:

Library Rules and Regulations:
• All Staff and Students are the members of our College Library.
• All students are eligible to borrow 18 Books.
• All staff are eligible to borrow Books.
• Reference books and periodicals will NOT be issued.
• Library ID is not transferable.
• Member should notify the Librarian any loss of cards and change of address immediately.
• The User may reserve a book in circulation. He will be notified as soon as the reserved book is returned. The book will be
retained at the circulation desk for one day from the date of return.
• Books will be issued for a short duration of 30 days only.
Fine Structure for Overdue Books:
• After 30 days — First 7 days (days 31–37): Rs. 1.00 per day per book
• After 30 days — 8 to 14 days (days 38–44): Rs. 2.00 per day per book
• After 30 days — 15 days onwards (day 45+): Rs. 5.00 per day per book
Additional Rules:
• Silence should be observed in the Library.
• Users should leave personal belongings (bags, briefcase, notebooks, files) at the entrance.
• Loss of books must be reported immediately to the Librarian. If the borrower is unable to replace the lost book, the cost (double
amount) will be recovered from the borrower.
• All books must be returned to the Library in time for physical stock verification.
• Students are advised to check whether the book contains all pages intact before borrowing. At the time of returning, if any
damage or defect is found, the borrower will be held responsible.

8. Industry Institution Interaction (III) Cell — Objectives, MoUs and Industries Visited

I This chunk covers the III Cell objectives, complete list of 43 MoUs signed with industries from 2017 to 2023, and a selected list of
industries visited by MSAJCE students.
MSAJCE Industry Institution Interaction (III) Cell: Technical institutes must bridge the gap between industry and academia. In a
competitive market due to increasing globalization of business, MSAJCE III Cell collaborates with industries to fulfil mutual
needs. MSAJCE-III Cell helps students and faculty understand present industrial expectations and relevant skill sets, identifies
skill gaps and provides upgrade opportunities, and enables faculty to train students to meet industrial needs.
III Cell Objectives: (1) Sign MoUs with industries for mutual benefit. (2) Organize workshops, conferences, seminars, guest
lectures and symposia. (3) Encourage faculty to undergo industry training. (4) Engage industrial experts to interact with students.
(5) Involve industrial experts in value-added course development. (6) Arrange industrial visits, internships and projects. (7)
Encourage professional consultancy by faculty. (8) Arrange faculty development programs. (9) Organize placement drives. (10)
Establish industry-oriented labs.

1. R&D Cell — Objectives

Describes the purpose and objectives of the MSAJCE Research and Development Cell, including focus areas, funding agency support,
and activities promoted.
Research and Development — MSAJCE
The Research and Development Cell aims to nurture research culture in the College by promoting research in newly emerging
and challenging areas of Engineering, Technology, Science and Humanities.
Objectives:
1. To encourage students and faculty to carry out research in Engineering, Technology, Science and Humanities by providing
necessary facilities and infrastructure.
2. To create zeal among students and faculty towards research and innovation and to encourage them to publish findings in
conferences and journals.
3. To assist students to apply for funding under the student project scheme to funding agencies like TNSCST, MSME, IEI (I) etc.
4. To work closely with industry to understand their needs, resulting in new or improved products, processes, systems or
services, and to promote Institute-Industry Collaboration.
5. To support the government by taking up sponsored projects offered by agencies such as TNSCST, DST, AICTE, UGC, ISRO,
DRDO, CSIR, DBT etc.
6. To enhance the general research capability of budding engineers by participating in conferences, seminars, workshops, and
project competitions.
7. To organize workshops, seminars, and trainings related to promotion of research.
8. To encourage both students and faculty to apply for copyrights and patents.
Key funding agencies supported: TNSCST, MSME, IEI (I), DST, AICTE, UGC, ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, DBT.

8. National Innovation and Start-up Policy (NISP) — Vision, Mission, Objectives and Committee

Details the MSAJCE National Innovation and Start-up Policy including vision, mission, short/long-term objectives, and the NISP
committee members with designations.
National Innovation and Start-up Policy (NISP) — MSAJCE
Vision:
To cater to the needs of student entrepreneurs with innovative ideas, thereby introducing a culture of entrepreneurship inside
campus which will strengthen the education system and promote national economic and social growth.
Mission:
To develop an ecosystem with required infrastructure that can enable students and faculty to innovate and prototype their
potential ideas with industrial standards and support from Government, industry and reputed academic institutions around the
world, and help them to realize their potentials.
Short Term Objectives:
1. To help student groups to prototype their ideas.
2. To improve innovation, creative and design thinking among student community.
3. Incubation facility for faculty-driven start-up and student/Alumni start-up.
4. Organize FDP, seminars, workshops, and distinguished talks for students, Faculty and Alumni to promote entrepreneurial
culture.
5. Strengthen institute-industry interaction cell activity and effectively use outcomes for achieving the mission.
Long Term Objectives:
1. Associate with DST, CII, MSME and other academic institutions for transferring world-class facility for MSAJCE IEDC
activities.

2. Improve quality of research work among students and attain patents that can be commercially used in production.
3. Provide a platform for students to develop innovative products with global recognition and generate business opportunities.
4. Generate revenues through consultancy work and student start-ups.
5. Spread awareness to students and faculty regarding IPR related activities.
6. Strategic partnership linkage with:
a. Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India (EDII), Chennai.
b. National Innovation Foundation (NIF) of India to submit ideas and apply for schemes.
c. Procure fund from AICTE for Entrepreneurship Development Cell.

Institution Innovation Council (IIC-MSAJCE)
IIC-MSAJCE was constituted as per the guidelines of the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) Innovation Cell
(MIC).
Introduction:
MHRD, Govt. of India established 'MHRD's Innovation Cell (MIC)' to systematically foster the culture of Innovation amongst all
Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). MIC's primary mandate is to encourage, inspire and nurture young students by supporting
them to work with new ideas and transform them into prototypes during their formative years.
MIC has envisioned creating 'Institution's Innovation Council (IICs)' across selected HEIs to promote a local innovation
ecosystem.
Major Focus of IIC:
• Create a vibrant local innovation ecosystem
• Start-up supporting mechanism in HEIs
• Prepare institute for Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA)
• Establish functional ecosystem for scouting ideas and pre-incubation of ideas
• Develop better Cognitive Ability for Technology Students
Functions of IICs:
• Identify and reward innovations and share success stories
• Organize periodic workshops/seminars/interactions with entrepreneurs, investors and professionals
• Network with peers and national entrepreneurship development organizations
• Create an Institution's Innovation portal to highlight innovative projects

• Organize Hackathons, idea competitions, mini-challenges with industry involvement

1. Department Overview, Vision and Mission

Overview of the S&H; department established in 2000, its role in engineering foundation, vision, mission and noted activities.
Department of Science and Humanities (S&H;) — MSAJCE
The department of S&H; was started in the year 2000. This department lays the base for furthering into one's engineering
career. Well experienced faculty with four doctorates contribute much in developing and moulding the students in enhancing
their knowledge to comprehend the basic subjects for better exposure. Students are guided through with innovative teaching
methods to make learning enjoyable. The laboratories available are well equipped to put into practice what the students have
learnt in theory classes. In addition to Literary and Debating Club activity, students are also exposed to various activities like
NSS, YRC, Physical Education and Yoga. The department holds the responsibility in making student-teacher and parent-teacher
interaction possible.
Vision:
To be a centre of excellence for transforming students into proficient engineers through sustainable problems.
Mission:
• M1. Impart fundamental knowledge and necessary skills in Science & Humanities through innovative teaching and learning
methodology
• M2. Inculcate critical thinking, ethics, lifelong learning and creativity needed for Industry and Society
• M3. Cultivate the students with all-round competencies, for career, higher education and self-employability

This club maintains records of sports and games events attended by students within the college, within the university and

MSAJCE Science Club
Introduction:
The Science Club was started with an aim to invite eminent scientists who would share their experience with students and
motivate them to gain scientific knowledge. Activities are designed primarily to introduce students to undertake interesting and
exciting science and technology projects. The Science Club consists of a group of students who want to explore the many
branches of engineering, mathematics, and science. The club is open to all students.
The purpose of the Science Club is to promote interest, understanding, and knowledge of the scientific world amongst college
students and the local community. Science Club is one of the largest clubs in the college. The club is divided into three sections:
Physics, Chemistry, and General.
The club aims to arouse engineering students' interest in learning science, promoting academic achievement in Science
subjects. It also helps students to learn more about science outside the classroom and teaches how to apply scientific
knowledge in daily life through activities. The club also guides students to develop an independent, logical and creative mind.
Activities include experiments in: making electronic components, making invisible ink, electroplating, biodiesels, fire writing, and
making venation of leaves. Information about the science club and day-to-day updates are displayed on the notice board.
Objectives of Science Club:
The five Guiding Principles govern how activities have been developed. Investigator activity offers students the opportunity to:
1. Solve a relevant, science-based problem set within a scenario.
2. Work in pairs or small groups or independently.
3. Take part in practical, hands-on science activities.
4. Think and talk about science during the activity and when sharing results.
5. Share results using a variety of media.
Things to Do in Science Club:

• Conduct Seminars, Workshops, Exhibitions and Quiz competitions to inculcate knowledge in the field of science.
• Make students acquire knowledge by giving lectures once a month.
• Promote the use of IT in learning science.
• Encourage student participation in activities organized by the Science Club.
• Help students promote discussion on recent innovations in the field of science once a month.
• Decorate the walls of the classroom, library and laboratory with scientific pictures and charts prepared by students themselves.

MSAJCE Tamil Mandram (Tamil Language and Culture Club)
Introduction:
The Tamil Mandram was formed to bring about a wonderful transformation in the youth to keep the Tamil language alive and
thriving. The motto of the Mandram is:
"Thithikkum then tamil mozhi endrum vaazha vendum! Engum vella vendum!"
(Translation: "The sweet honey Tamil language must live forever! Must win everywhere!")
The Mandram works to revive and reconstruct the ancient Tamil culture and the identities left behind by ancestors. The vision is
for the youth to take pride in their language and move from just speaking Tamil to actively bringing glory to Tamil through action.
"Vaazha Tamil! Velga Tamil!"
(Translation: "Long live Tamil! Victory to Tamil!")
Objectives of Tamil Mandram:
1. To develop Tamil enthusiasm and knowledge among students — this is the primary objective of the Tamil Mandram.
2. To spread ancient Tamil culture and heritage among today's youth.
3. To develop technical knowledge in Tamil.
4. To continuously conduct Tamil events and social activities suited to the times.
Events Conducted by Tamil Mandram:
1. Irumugam Oru Agam (Two faces, one heart — elocution/drama)
2. Pessum Padam (Speaking Picture — storytelling)
3. Aadu Puli (Tiger and Goat — traditional game)
4. Kaivanna Kaviyam (Colourful Poetry — art and poetry)
5. Tent Kottai (Tent Camp — cultural event)
6. Vidugadhai Vilaiyattu (Riddle Games)

7. Pirasangatin Thalaiwan (King of Speeches — debate/oratory competition)
8. Tamilkkorvai (Tamil Chain — literary event)

About:
Programming abilities are crucial tools that can be applied to and integrated into a variety of disciplines and domains in today's
climate of rapid change.
Aim:
1. More coding contests should be held to reach all students on campus.
2. Conduct workshops on computer science topics like web development, application development, machine learning, IoT, etc.

MSAJCE Energy and Eco Club
Energy Club:
The goal of the Energy Club is to raise and spread knowledge about responsible and sustainable energy use. Given the limited
quantity of fossil fuels available, resource management and conservation are urgently needed. Students are introduced to the
concept of energy conservation through the Energy Club, as well as the necessity for it and what part they can play in
guaranteeing conservation. In order to combat the ongoing energy issue, it helps the students to conserve energy. These
actions would support not only the dissemination of information about energy efficiency but also its application in homes and
institutions.
Eco Club:
The Eco Club holds that nature imparts life lessons in its own steady ways and empowers our young students to share their
responsibility for upholding environmental health and taking action to prevent environmental degradation both individually and
collectively. The club encourages students to take both individual and collective action to protect the environment.

MSAJCE Photography Club
Introduction:
The members of the photography club are encouraged to take images as they grow to appreciate the hobby more. It gives
workers and students a venue for exploring and appreciating their surroundings through photography, short filmmaking, and
screenwriting.

There is much more to photography than just using a camera to take photographs. By comprehending and learning about what
constitutes a successful photograph — from composition to creative expression — students in this club have the chance to
develop their skills. Additionally, club members will learn how to edit and improve photographs using cutting-edge software for
both personal use and publication.
While taking pictures of sporting events and activities relevant to the school, students are encouraged to hone their talents.
Exploring this fascinating aspect of the visual arts is welcomed and encouraged for people of all expertise levels.
Key Skills Developed:
1. Photography composition and creative expression
2. Photo editing using advanced software
3. Short filmmaking and screenwriting
4. Event photography (sports events, college activities)
5. Visual arts exploration
The club is open to all expertise levels — beginners and advanced photographers are both welcome.

1. CSBS Department Overview, Key Features & Programme Details

B.Tech in Computer Science and Business Systems (CSBS) is a specialized undergraduate engineering program designed to
blend core computer science education with insights into business systems and management. Introduced in collaboration with
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) to bridge the gap between traditional computer science education and the dynamic needs of
the IT and business world in the era of Business 4.0.
Curriculum covers: Analytics, Deep Learning, Machine Learning, Cloud Computing, Business Analytics, Financial Management,
Economics, Internet of Things, Design Thinking, humanities and value-added science.
Key Features:
• Balanced Curriculum — Core CS (Data Structures, Algorithms, OS, DBMS, AI/ML) + Business subjects (Economics, Financial
Management, Business Process Management).
• Industry Collaboration — Designed in partnership with TCS; emphasis on employability and industry readiness.
• Focus Areas — Problem-solving using computational thinking, Business analytics, IT systems for business applications.
• Soft Skills Training — Communication, Teamwork, Entrepreneurial thinking.
Benefits Over Regular CSE: More interdisciplinary exposure; better suited for tech-enabled business functions; greater
alignment with industry expectations in IT services and consulting.

Department of Computer Science and Engineering — MSAJCE
Computer Science and Engineering is one of the popular courses among engineering students. It mainly focuses on
programming, computation, analysis of algorithm, program design and testing, software engineering etc for design, development
and analysis of software and hardware used to solve the problem of various businesses, scientific and social issues. CSE
integrates both computer hardware and software and is intended to develop solid understanding of the entire computer system
and its accessories and software. It provides sophistication to the world and touches human lives in all aspects such as
education, transportation, entertainment, banking, social media, healthcare and supply chain management. CSE is an
interdisciplinary subject linked with psychology, geology science, maths, art, music, bio informatics, electronics, and operation
research.

2025–2030.
Job Opportunities in India and Abroad (Both Public & Private Sectors)
Job opportunities for CSE are available in over 50% of all available jobs in engineering. In India, 60% of jobs are available in the
IT sector (both private and public sector).
Public Sector: Railways, Airport, ONGC, Remote Sensing, Banking Sector, etc.
Private Sector: TCS, Infosys, CTS, Wipro, HCL Technology, Tech Mahindra, Zoho, Intel, Accenture, IBM, FSS, etc.
Employment Growth in Computer Science and Engineering (2025–2030):
The employment opportunities for CSE in India over the next five years are expected to be highly promising due to the growing
demand for technological innovation, digitalization, adoption of advanced technologies, and India's strong position as a global IT
hub.
Key Drivers of Employment Growth:
1. Digital Transformation Across Industries — Digital India Initiative, Smart Cities, IoT, Automation and AI Adoption.
2. Rise of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning — AI/ML central to healthcare, finance, retail, logistics; India's AI market
expected to grow rapidly.
3. Cyber Security — Increasing cyber threats; demand for cybersecurity experts projected to rise. Government enforcing
stronger data protection (Personal Data Protection Bill).
4. Cloud Computing and DevOps — Cloud adoption (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud); DevOps practices for automating software
development.
5. Big Data and Data Science — Data-driven decision making; demand for data scientists, data engineers, and BI experts.
6. Blockchain and Fintech — Blockchain in supply chain, financial services, smart contracts; India's fintech sector booming.
7. Internet of Things (IoT) — Smart devices in healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, home automation.
8. 5G Technology and Networking — 5G rollout in India; demand for software engineers and network specialists.
9. E-Commerce and Digital Content — Growth of e-commerce platforms; gaming, streaming, AR/VR market expansion.

# B.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science

## 1. Overview
The B.Tech program in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science provides a comprehensive education in these rapidly growing fields. Artificial intelligence is the process of creating machines to think like humans. It is a term used to describe the simulation of human intelligence processes in machines. It typically involves sophisticated algorithms that enable computers to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, and decision making.

Data Science is a field of knowledge which applies advanced statistical and mathematical techniques to large datasets in order to extract knowledge from them. This data can be structured like a spreadsheet but can also be unstructured like text or video data. Data science is the application of techniques from statistics, mathematics, computer programming, and other fields to solve real-world problems using information technology.

Due to the exploration of the Internet, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science deliver data-driven solutions using computational principles, methods, and systems for extracting information from data and modern computational systems that reveal capabilities of insight, way of thinking, learning, and action that are typical of human intelligence.

Since 2015, the B.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science has emerged as one of the most high-growth, dynamic, and lucrative careers in technology. This course aims at providing not only the core technologies such as artificial intelligence, data mining, and data modeling but also gives intensive inputs in areas of machine learning and big data analytics. Through this course, the students will gain cross-disciplinary skills across fields such as statistics, computer science, machine learning, and logic. Graduates may have career opportunities in healthcare, business, e-commerce, social networking companies, climatology, biotechnology, genetics, and other important areas. The major focus of this programme is to equip students with statistical, mathematical reasoning, machine learning, knowledge discovery, and visualization skills.

The specialized branch deals with the core principles and ethical issues in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence and motivates students to explore the cutting-edge applications related to Big Data, Neural Networks, and Deep Learning. Applications like Alexa, Siri, Erica, Sophia, Tesla’s driverless car, and Chat-bots are becoming common. AI-powered robots can take over human life-endangering jobs like firefighting, deep-sea oil drilling, mining works with high mortality rates, and more.

## 2. Career Opportunities
The career opportunities for Artificial Intelligence and Data Science graduates are vast across various sectors such as manufacturing, software, research, education, defense, banking and finance, e-commerce, transport, and health science. Specific roles include software engineer, software tester, application developer, information and multimedia designer, medical information scientist, technology developer, IT specialist, technical consultant, quality analyst, information network manager, and data quality analyst.

## 3. Vision
The vision of the department is to be a center of excellence for transforming students into proficient Artificial Intelligence and Data Science professionals through sustainable practices.

## 4. Mission
The mission involves imparting core fundamental knowledge and necessary skills in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science through innovative teaching and learning methodologies. It also focuses on inculcating critical thinking, ethics, lifelong learning, and creativity needed for industry and society. Furthermore, the mission aims to cultivate the students with all-round competencies for their career, higher education, and self-employability.

## 5. Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs)
- **Programme Educational Objective (PEO1)**: The Programme Educational Objectives are designed to ensure that graduates will be prepared for analyzing, designing, developing, and testing software solutions and products with creativity and sustainability. - **Programme Educational Objective (PEO2)**: Graduates will also be skilled in the use of modern tools for critical problem solving and analyzing industrial and societal requirements. - **Programme Educational Objective (PEO3)**: Additionally, they will be prepared with managerial and leadership skills for their career and for starting up their own firms.

## 6. Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
- **Program Specific Outcome (PSO1)**: The Program Specific Outcomes state that engineering graduates will be able to develop creative solutions by adapting emerging technologies and tools for real-time applications in the industry. - **Program Specific Outcome (PSO2)**: They will also apply their acquired knowledge to develop software solutions and innovative mobile apps for various automation applications.

## 7. Programme Outcomes (PO)
The Programme Outcomes define the foundational abilities of the students. - **Programme Outcome (PO1) - Engineering Knowledge**: Engineering knowledge requires applying mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to solve complex engineering problems. - **Programme Outcome (PO2) - Problem Analysis**: Problem analysis involves identifying, formulating, reviewing research literature, and analyzing complex engineering problems to reach substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences. - **Programme Outcome (PO3) - Design/Development of Solutions**: For the design and development of solutions, students must design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, as well as cultural, societal, and environmental considerations. - **Programme Outcome (PO4) - Conduct Investigations**: Conducting investigations of complex problems requires using research-based knowledge and methods, including the design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of information to provide valid conclusions. - **Programme Outcome (PO5) - Modern Tool Usage**: Modern tool usage involves creating, selecting, and applying appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools, including prediction and modeling, to complex engineering activities with an understanding of their limitations.

- **Programme Outcome (PO6) - The Engineer and Society**: Further Programme Outcomes emphasize the engineer and society, applying reasoning informed by contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to professional engineering practice. - **Programme Outcome (PO7) - Environment and Sustainability**: Environment and sustainability focus on understanding the impact of professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, demonstrating the knowledge of and need for sustainable development. - **Programme Outcome (PO8) - Ethics**: Ethics involves applying ethical principles and committing to professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of engineering practice. - **Programme Outcome (PO9) - Individual and Team Work**: Individual and teamwork require functioning effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multidisciplinary settings. - **Programme Outcome (PO10) - Communication**: Communication ensures the ability to communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and society at large, including comprehending and writing effective reports, designing documentation, making effective presentations, and giving and receiving clear instructions. - **Programme Outcome (PO11) - Project Management and Finance**: Project management and finance involve demonstrating knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles and applying these to one's own work, managing projects, and working in multidisciplinary environments. - **Programme Outcome (PO12) - Life-long Learning**: Finally, life-long learning recognizes the need for and the ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

## 8. Job Profiles

### AI and Data Science Growth in India by 2025 – 2030
The Artificial Intelligence and Data Science sectors in India are experiencing explosive growth expected between 2025 and 2030. As AI-driven solutions rely on data analytics to make better decisions, the demand for professionals in these fields is expected to grow significantly. This growth is driven by increased AI adoption across industries such as healthcare, finance, e-commerce, telecommunications, automotive, and manufacturing. AI will be used for tasks like predictive analytics, personalized services, data-driven decision-making, and automation, integrating into core business functions like human resources, finance, and customer service. Government support and initiatives, such as Digital India, the National AI Strategy, and the National AI Mission, further boost AI research, startups, and adoption across public services, making India a global leader in AI for smart cities, healthcare, and agriculture. The rising demand for data-driven decision-making leads to advancements in customer segmentation, fraud detection, and supply chain optimization. The growth in AI-powered startups is expected to double, creating numerous job opportunities for engineers, data scientists, and product managers as industries increasingly adopt AI-based automation to streamline operations, reduce costs, and offer personalized customer experiences.

### Key AI and Data Science Job Roles in India (2025-2030)
Key Artificial Intelligence and Data Science job roles in India include Data Scientists who analyze large data sets to derive actionable insights, build predictive models, and help organizations make data-driven decisions. This role requires skills in Python, R, SQL, machine learning algorithms, statistical analysis, data visualization tools like Tableau and Power BI, and deep learning. The demand for data scientists will remain high across healthcare, finance, retail, and e-commerce. Machine Learning Engineers build and deploy machine learning models, implement algorithms, and optimize model performance for real-world applications. They require skills in Python, TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch, neural networks, cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, along with algorithm optimization. The demand for machine learning engineers will rise as companies adopt more AI solutions, especially in startups and tech giants.

AI Research Scientists conduct cutting-edge research in AI, focusing on deep learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, and natural language processing. Their skill set includes machine learning algorithms, Python, mathematical modeling, research publications, and deep learning frameworks. Growing AI investments from global tech companies and research labs will result in high demand for AI research scientists. Data Analysts collect, process, and analyze data to uncover trends, create dashboards, and support decision-making with data-driven insights. They need skills in Excel, SQL, Python, data visualization tools, and statistical tools like R and SAS. As companies focus on data-driven decision-making, the demand for data analysts in sectors like finance, retail, and healthcare will increase.

Data Engineers design, construct, and maintain large-scale data pipelines, working with big data technologies to ensure data is stored, processed, and accessible. They require skills in SQL, Python, Hadoop, Spark, Kafka, cloud services, and ETL processes. The growth of big data and cloud computing will drive the demand for data engineers in data-driven companies. AI Product Managers oversee the development and deployment of AI-powered products and manage cross-functional teams of engineers and data scientists. They must be skilled in product lifecycle management, agile methodologies, machine learning, project management, and business strategy. The rise in AI product development across industries will create more opportunities for AI product managers.

Business Intelligence Developers design and develop tools to collect, store, and analyze business data to help businesses make strategic decisions using AI-driven insights. They need skills in SQL, Power BI, Tableau, data visualization, reporting tools, and Python. The shift to data-driven strategies will increase the demand for BI developers, particularly in e-commerce and retail. Natural Language Processing Engineers work on algorithms and models that allow machines to process and understand human language, such as chatbots, virtual assistants, and sentiment analysis. They require skills in Python, NLP frameworks like NLTK, SpaCy, and Hugging Face, machine learning, deep learning, and text mining. The rise of AI chatbots and text analytics will grow the demand for NLP engineers in e-commerce, finance, and telecommunications.

### Industry-Specific AI and Data Science Job Trends
Industry-specific Artificial Intelligence and Data Science job trends span multiple sectors. In healthcare, there is a focus on diagnostics, personalized treatment, drug discovery, robot-assisted surgery, bioinformatics, healthcare data analysis, and medical AI applications. The finance and fintech sectors utilize AI for fraud detection, credit scoring, automated trading, and personalized financial services within banks, insurance companies, and fintech startups. E-commerce and retail focus on personalization, dynamic pricing, inventory optimization, and recommendation systems. The automotive and autonomous vehicles sector is advancing in autonomous driving, vehicle-to-everything communication, predictive maintenance, computer vision, sensor data processing, and AI-powered automotive solutions. The telecommunication sector is prioritizing network optimization, customer service chatbots, predictive maintenance, 5G, the Internet of Things, and edge computing.

### Expected Growth and Salary Trends
The job market growth for Artificial Intelligence and Data Science in India is expected to grow at a Compound Annual Growth Rate of thirty to forty percent. By 2030, India could see hundreds of thousands of AI and data science job openings in tech companies, startups, and industries adopting data-driven transformation. Salary trends for these roles are highly competitive. Entry-level roles for zero to two years of experience typically range from 6 to 12 Lakhs per annum. Mid-level roles for three to five years of experience range from 12 to 25 Lakhs per annum. Senior-level roles for over five years of experience can range from 25 to 50 Lakhs per annum. AI Research Scientists often see salaries ranging from 30 to 70 Lakhs per annum.

### Skills and Certifications Required
To succeed in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science jobs, professionals require a strong foundation of skills and certifications. Key skills include Python, R, and SQL for data manipulation and machine learning algorithms. Professionals must be proficient in machine learning frameworks like TensorFlow, Keras, and PyTorch. Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure is essential for deploying AI models. Additionally, expertise in big data tools like Hadoop, Spark, and Kafka is critical. Candidates are encouraged to pursue advanced certifications from platforms like Coursera, edX, and Udacity. Highly regarded certifications include the Google Professional Machine Learning Engineer, AWS Certified Machine Learning Specialty, the Data Science Specialization by IBM, and the Deep Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng.

# Anti-Ragging Policy at Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering (**MSAJCE**), Siruseri, Chennai

The Anti-Ragging Policy at Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering (**MSAJCE**) in Siruseri, Chennai, strictly prohibits any indiscipline activities by students that cause or are likely to cause annoyance, hardship, physical or psychological harm, or raise fear or apprehension in any fresher or other student. It is strictly forbidden to ask any student to perform acts they would not ordinarily do, especially those that generate a sense of shame, torment, or embarrassment affecting their physical or psychological well-being. Furthermore, **MSAJCE** explicitly bans any acts by senior students that prevent, disrupt, or disturb the regular academic activities of freshers or other students. Exploiting the services of any student to complete academic tasks assigned to an individual or group is also considered a severe violation of the policy.

The anti-ragging framework comprehensively covers and prohibits any acts of financial extortion or forceful expenditure burdens placed on freshers or other students. The policy maintains a zero-tolerance approach toward any physical abuse, encompassing all its variants such as sexual abuse, homosexual assaults, stripping, forcing obscene and lewd acts or gestures, causing bodily harm, or posing any danger to health or person. Additionally, any abuse through spoken words, emails, posts, or public insults is strictly penalized, especially acts involving deriving perverted pleasure, or a vicarious or sadistic thrill from actively or passively participating in the discomfiture of a fresher or any other student. Finally, **MSAJCE** strictly forbids any acts that affect the mental health and self-confidence of a student, whether or not the intent is to derive sadistic pleasure or to show off power, authority, or superiority over others.

## 1. Punishments and Disciplinary Actions

Students found guilty of ragging at **MSAJCE** face severe disciplinary actions and punishments. The administration reserves the right to withhold or withdraw scholarships, fellowships, and any other associated benefits from the offenders. Guilty individuals may be debarred from appearing in any tests, examinations, or other evaluation processes, and their academic results may be formally withheld. Furthermore, offenders can be debarred from representing **MSAJCE** in any regional, national, or international meets, tournaments, or youth festivals.

More severe consequences for ragging violations include immediate suspension or expulsion from **MSAJCE** hostel, as well as the outright cancellation of their admission to **MSAJCE**. Depending on the severity of the offense, the administration may rusticate the student from **MSAJCE** for a period ranging from one to four semesters. In the most extreme cases, the punishment involves permanent expulsion from **MSAJCE**, along with consequent debarring from admission to any other educational institution for a specified period.

# Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)

## 1. Overview
Computer Science and Engineering is one of the most popular courses among engineering students. It mainly focuses on programming, computation, analysis of algorithms, program design and testing, and software engineering for the design, development, and analysis of software and hardware used to solve the problems of various businesses, scientific, and social issues. Computer Science and Engineering integrates both computer hardware and software, intending to develop a solid understanding of the entire computer system, its accessories, and software. It provides sophistication to the world and touches human lives in all aspects, such as education, transportation, entertainment, banking, social media, healthcare, and supply chain management. This field is an interdisciplinary subject incorporating elements from psychology, geology, science, mathematics, art, music, bioinformatics, electronics, and operations research. The study helps students understand how computer science fits into a wide range of domains in the world.

Sectors with high employment potential include IT Services and Software Development, which require software engineers, web developers, and mobile app developers. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning adoption in healthcare, finance, e-commerce, and logistics requires a large workforce of AI and ML engineers and data scientists. Cybersecurity and the rapid growth of Fintech and Blockchain in India will drive the demand for software developers and blockchain engineers. ## 8. Job Profiles

### Employment Growth in Cyber Security in India by 2025 - 2030
The cybersecurity sector in India is expected to experience strong growth over the next five years due to the increasing frequency and sophistication of cyber attacks, the rapid digitization of businesses, and the expansion of digital infrastructures in various industries. As businesses and government organizations continue to embrace digital transformation, the demand for cybersecurity professionals will rise significantly.

### Key Drivers of Employment Growth
Increasing cybersecurity threats are a primary driver, as more data moves online, necessitating experts to design secure systems, prevent data breaches, and mitigate risks. Government initiatives and regulations, such as the Personal Data Protection Bill, the National Cyber Security Strategy, and best practices in data security, create more demand for professionals. Agencies like CERT-In and NCIIPC push for enhanced cybersecurity protocols, encouraging private sector adoption. The growth of cloud computing and IoT also fuels demand; as companies migrate to the cloud, professionals skilled in platforms like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud are highly sought after. The rise of IoT devices across sectors creates a need for developers to design secure systems. In digital payments and financial services, the fintech boom and stricter regulations from authorities like the RBI and SEBI require professionals to protect systems and ensure GDPR compliance. Furthermore, the digital transformation across industries, propelled by initiatives like Digital India, smart cities, and the adoption of AI and automation, continuously boosts the demand for cybersecurity experts.

### Employment Opportunities in High Demand
A Cybersecurity Analyst monitors network traffic, identifies security breaches, and implements protective measures, utilizing skills in network security, incident response, SIEM tools, firewall management, and penetration testing. A Security Architect designs and implements complex security infrastructures to protect IT systems, networks, and data, requiring expertise in network architecture, security frameworks, risk management, cloud security, firewalls, and encryption technologies. A Penetration Tester or Ethical Hacker conducts tests to identify and exploit vulnerabilities, simulating cyber attacks using tools like Kali Linux, Metasploit, Wireshark, nmap, and vulnerability scanning tools. A Security Operations Center Analyst monitors networks for threats and responds to incidents in real-time, relying on skills in threat analysis, log analysis, incident detection, and SIEM systems. A Cloud Security Specialist ensures the security of cloud infrastructures and applications, focusing on preventing unauthorized access and data breaches with skills in AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and IAM.

A Cybersecurity Consultant provides expertise to organizations on improving their overall security posture by assessing vulnerabilities and recommending solutions, which requires skills in risk assessment, security audits, compliance frameworks, and policy development. An Incident Responder investigates and responds to cybersecurity incidents like data breaches and malware attacks, utilizing incident handling, forensics, malware analysis, and root cause analysis. A Cybersecurity Engineer builds and maintains security systems, firewalls, and encryption technologies to protect assets, requiring skills in firewall configuration, endpoint protection, and network security protocols. The Chief Information Security Officer oversees an organization's entire cybersecurity strategy, policies, systems, and incident response, ensuring compliance with regulations and requiring strong leadership, risk management, and business continuity planning skills. Finally, an IoT Security Expert protects connected devices in IoT ecosystems from cyber threats, ensuring encryption and security through knowledge of IoT protocols and embedded security.

### Sectors with High Employment Potential
Sectors with high employment potential include IT and IT Services, where companies need experts to protect their systems and those of their clients. Financial Services and Fintech sectors, including banks and digital payment providers, invest heavily in cybersecurity to safeguard transactions and comply with regulations. The E-Commerce sector requires professionals to protect customer data and payment systems from threats. Government and Defense sectors focus on digital governance and smart cities, increasing the need to protect critical infrastructures. Telecommunications companies need network security experts to protect data as 5G technology rolls out. Healthcare requires specialists to secure sensitive health records and telemedicine systems. Finally, Cloud Services providers need professionals skilled in securing cloud platforms and ensuring compliance with data protection laws.

### Key Skills Required for Cyber security Roles
Network security requires an understanding of TCP/IP, network protocols, firewalls, and proficiency in tools like Wireshark, nmap, and Snort. Ethical hacking and penetration testing involve skills to simulate cyberattacks and uncover vulnerabilities using Kali Linux, Metasploit, Burp Suite, Nessus, and Aircrack-ng. Cloud security demands knowledge of securing environments like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, along with IAM and encryption. Incident response and forensics require skills to detect, respond, and recover from breaches, using digital forensics tools. Data encryption and cryptography involve understanding encryption methods like AES, OpenSSL, and GPG to protect data. Risk management and compliance require evaluating potential risks and understanding frameworks like ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI DSS. Proficiency in SIEM tools such as Splunk, IBM QRadar, or ArcSight is necessary for real-time monitoring. Security automation and scripting require knowledge of tools like Puppet or Ansible and languages like Python or Bash. Threat intelligence involves analyzing and responding to emerging cyber threats. Lastly, understanding security in IoT and mobile devices is becoming increasingly important as these technologies become more pervasive.

### Cybersecurity Certifications
Certifications can greatly enhance credibility and job prospects in the cybersecurity field. Notable certifications include the Certified Ethical Hacker by EC-Council, the Certified Information Systems Security Professional by ISC2, the Certified Information Security Manager and the Certified Information Systems Auditor by ISACA, and CompTIA Security+. Other valuable certifications are the Certified Cloud Security Professional by ISC2, the Certified Penetration Testing Engineer and the Certified SOC Analyst by EC-Council, the Cisco Certified CyberOps Associate, and the GIAC Security Essentials.

### Learning Paths for Cyber security Careers
For beginners, the focus is on network security basics, firewall setup, and vulnerability scanning, often pursuing certifications like CompTIA Security+ and CEH Foundation through online platforms. At the intermediate level, the focus shifts to advanced network security, cloud security, penetration testing, and risk management, targeting certifications like CISSP, CISM, and CCSP through more in-depth training resources. Advanced level professionals focus on ethical hacking, security management, and incident response, aiming for certifications like CISA and CPTE through specialized training from organizations like EC-Council, GIAC, and the SANS Institute.

### Additional Resources to Enhance Your Skills
Additional resources include participating in Capture The Flag challenges on platforms like Hack The Box, TryHackMe, and OverTheWire to practice penetration testing and cryptography. Following cybersecurity blogs and podcasts like Krebs On Security, Dark Reading, and the SANS Internet Storm Center helps stay updated on trends. Attending webinars and conferences like Black Hat, DEFCON, and the RSA Conference is excellent for networking and learning about emerging threats. Familiarizing oneself with open-source tools like Wireshark, Metasploit, Kali Linux, and Burp Suite is also highly recommended.

### Top Online Cybersecurity Courses
Top online courses include CompTIA Security+ for beginners, Certified Ethical Hacker for aspiring penetration testers, and Cisco CCNA Security for those interested in network security. Other advanced courses include the Certified Information Systems Security Professional for managerial roles, the Certified Cloud Security Professional for cloud computing, and GIAC Security Essentials for strengthening foundational skills. There are also comprehensive specializations offered by universities on platforms like Coursera, such as the Cybersecurity Specialization by the University of Maryland and the Cybersecurity for Business Specialization by the University of Colorado. Advanced learners can pursue Advanced Penetration Testing and Ethical Hacking through Offensive Security, while those seeking leadership roles can take the Certified Information Security Manager course.

### Free and Low-Cost Learning Resources
Free and low-cost learning resources include Cybrary, which offers courses ranging from beginner to advanced levels, and Udemy, which provides affordable courses on various topics. Coursera offers free courses on basic concepts from top universities, while SANS Cyber Aces provides introductory courses on network security and operating systems. OWASP offers open-source resources for web application security. TryHackMe and Hack The Box are excellent platforms for interactive, hands-on challenges. Additionally, YouTube channels like The Cyber Mentor, NetworkChuck, and Professor Messer provide valuable tutorials and study materials.

### Cybersecurity Career Path Resources
Career path resources include LinkedIn Learning for courses on fundamentals and risk management. Cybersecurity podcasts like Darknet Diaries, The CyberWire, and Security Now offer insights into real-world attacks and news. Communities on Reddit, Stack Exchange, and Twitter provide platforms for discussion, networking, and staying updated. Recommended books for deepening knowledge include The Web Application Hacker's Handbook by Dafydd Stuttard and Marcus Pinto, Hacking: The Art of Exploitation by Jon Erickson, and The CISSP All-in-One Exam Guide by Shon Harris.

While the park's mandate focuses on technology, it does not typically host traditional non-IT manufacturing (like textiles or heavy machinery), which are located in other SIPCOT complexes (e.g., Sriperumbudur or Oragadam).

Here is the comprehensive list of companies, brands, and infrastructure operating within the park as of 2026:

## Major IT & Software Services
These companies occupy the largest land parcels and form the core of the park:

- **Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)**: The largest occupant with over 70 acres and multiple buildings focused on IT services and R&D.
- **Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTS)**: Operates a massive campus (Plots B-40 to B-44) for digital solutions and BPO.
- **Capgemini**: Located in Plot H-6, focusing on engineering and digital transformation.
- **HCL Technologies**: Maintains a substantial campus for software development and infrastructure management.
- **Hexaware Technologies**: One of the early major tenants with a large dedicated facility.
- **Infosys**: Operates a significant development center within the park.
- **Atos** (formerly **Atos Syntel**): Continues operations following the acquisition of Syntel.
- **Aspire Systems**: Headquartered in the park (Plot 1/D-1), specializing in engineering and R&D services.
- **Polaris Software Lab** (part of **LTIMindtree**): A key early tenant focused on banking and financial software.
- **CareVoyant Technologies**: Located in Plot 26/A-39, specializing in home health software.
- **Placka Information Technologies**: Provides IT solutions from Plot 6/A-12.

## Data Centers & Digital Infrastructure
Siruseri has emerged as a critical data center hub with recent high-profile inaugurations:

- **Sify Technologies**: Inaugurated South India’s largest **AI-ready data center** campus in April 2025. The facility spans multiple towers with a total investment exceeding ₹10,000 crore, offering 130 MW capacity.
- **Equinix**: Opened its first Chennai International Business Exchange (**IBX**) data center (CN1) in September 2025. The ₹574 crore facility covers six acres, initially housing 800 cabinets (scalable to 4,250) with liquid cooling for AI workloads.

## Electronics, Defense & Specialized Manufacturing
While rare in this specific IT park, some high-tech manufacturing and defense electronics units are present:

- **Data Patterns (India) Limited**: Located at Plot No. H-9, this is a key **defense and aerospace** electronics manufacturer. Unlike typical IT firms, it engages in the design and production of advanced electronic subsystems for defense platforms.
- **FT8012 (Fidelity Technologies)**: Operates an innovation center within the park, often associated with financial technology hardware and specialized software solutions.

## Other Notable Entities
- **ETA Technopark**: A commercial technology complex located immediately adjacent/within the Siruseri stretch, often grouped with the SIPCOT ecosystem, housing various smaller tech firms and startups.
- **Polaris Financial Technologies**: Often listed separately due to its specific focus on financial software products before its merger into LTIMindtree.

> **Note on Non-IT Companies:** The SIPCOT IT Park in Siruseri is zoned specifically for **IT, ITES, Electronics, and Data Centers**. You will not find traditional non-IT brands (e.g., consumer goods, automotive assembly, textiles) here; those are located in nearby SIPCOT parks like **Sriperumbudur** (automotive) or **Oragadam** (manufacturing). The "non-IT" presence in Siruseri is limited to **defense electronics** (Data Patterns) and **facility management/support services** required to run the large campuses.

# Electronics and Communication Engineering with Specialization in Advanced Communication Technology

## 1. Overview
The B.Tech program in Electronics and Communication Engineering with a Specialization in Advanced Communication Technology, offered under the faculty of Electronics and Communication Engineering, has been framed based on NEP guidelines with a focus on multidisciplinary education. The objective of the program is to develop Advanced Communication Technology-based industry-competent professionals of global standard capable of accepting challenges and solving societal problems at a larger level. As the world becomes more digitized and the speed of communication becomes a critical factor, the evolution of 5G and 6G communication systems is imminent.

The program focuses on modern communication systems such as wireless and optical communication, RF and microwave communication, laser and light wave communication, and next-generation advanced communication technologies. The curriculum deeply covers massive multiple-input multiple-output, beamforming through advanced digital signal processing, device-to-device communication, millimeter-wave technologies, communication networks, embedded systems, the Internet of Things, cyber and network security, information theory and coding. Additionally, subjects like satellite communication, navigation systems, and quantum and molecular communication are also explored. A strong emphasis is placed throughout the course on developing practical skills and in-depth knowledge required by modern industries.

Through this course, students will have professional prospects in a range of industries, including network providers such as BSNL and AIRTEL, as well as in manufacturing, healthcare, education, the IT sector, civil aviation, defense, postal and railway departments, All India Radio and TV stations, the Indian Telecom Sector, the National Physics Lab, and numerous companies like Bharat Electronics Ltd, ONGC, SAIL, Cisco, Havells, 3M India, Reliance, Bajaj, Bosch, and Philips.

## 2. Programme
The program offered is a B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering with a Specialization in Advanced Communication Technology. The duration is four years for regular students and three years for lateral entry students, comprising eight and six semesters, respectively. The total intake is 30 seats, divided equally with 15 for the government quota and 15 for the management quota. Eligibility for the program requires completion of the 10+2 system of education, and students must have secured a pass in Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics in their qualifying examination. The curriculum and syllabus follow the 2021 Regulation. Opportunities are vast in public sector undertakings and the government sector. The scope for higher studies includes pursuing an M.E., M.Tech, or M.B.A.

## 3. Vision
The vision is to be a center of excellence for transforming students into proficient Communication Engineers through sustainable practices.

## 4. Mission
The mission involves imparting core fundamental knowledge and necessary skills in communication systems through innovative teaching and learning methodologies. It aims to inculcate the critical thinking, ethics, lifelong learning, and creativity needed for both the industry and society. Furthermore, the mission cultivates the students with all-around competencies for their careers, higher education, and self-employability.

## 5. Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs)
- **Programme Educational Objective (PEO1)**: The Programme Educational Objectives state that graduates will be prepared for analyzing, designing, developing, and testing software solutions and products with creativity and sustainability. They will also be skilled in the use of modern tools for critical problem solving and analyzing industrial and societal requirements. In addition, graduates will be prepared with managerial and leadership skills for their careers and for starting up their own firms.

## 6. Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
The Program Specific Outcomes emphasize that engineering graduates will be able to develop creative solutions by adapting emerging technologies and tools for real-time applications in the industry. - **Program Specific Outcome (PSO2)**: They will also apply their acquired knowledge to develop software solutions and innovative mobile apps for various automation applications.

## 7. Programme Outcomes (PO)
The Programme Outcomes define the foundational abilities of the students. - **Programme Outcome (PO1) - Engineering Knowledge**: Engineering knowledge requires applying mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to solve complex engineering problems. - **Programme Outcome (PO2) - Problem Analysis**: Problem analysis involves identifying, formulating, reviewing research literature, and analyzing complex engineering problems to reach substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences. - **Programme Outcome (PO3) - Design/Development of Solutions**: For the design and development of solutions, students must design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, as well as cultural, societal, and environmental considerations. - **Programme Outcome (PO4) - Conduct Investigations**: Conducting investigations of complex problems requires using research-based knowledge and methods, including the design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of information to provide valid conclusions. - **Programme Outcome (PO5) - Modern Tool Usage**: Modern tool usage involves creating, selecting, and applying appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools, including prediction and modeling, to complex engineering activities with an understanding of their limitations.

- **Programme Outcome (PO6) - The Engineer and Society**: Further Programme Outcomes emphasize the engineer and society, applying reasoning informed by contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to professional engineering practice. - **Programme Outcome (PO7) - Environment and Sustainability**: Environment and sustainability focus on understanding the impact of professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, demonstrating the knowledge of and need for sustainable development. - **Programme Outcome (PO8) - Ethics**: Ethics involves applying ethical principles and committing to professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of engineering practice. - **Programme Outcome (PO9) - Individual and Team Work**: Individual and teamwork require functioning effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multidisciplinary settings. - **Programme Outcome (PO10) - Communication**: Communication ensures the ability to communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and society at large, including comprehending and writing effective reports, designing documentation, making effective presentations, and giving and receiving clear instructions. - **Programme Outcome (PO11) - Project Management and Finance**: Project management and finance involve demonstrating knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles and applying these to one's own work, managing projects, and working in multidisciplinary environments. - **Programme Outcome (PO12) - Life-long Learning**: Finally, life-long learning recognizes the need for and the ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

## 8. Job Profiles
The job profiles for Electronics and Communication Engineers encompass various roles. A Design Engineer works on the research and design of new products for a company, drafting and testing prototypes to ensure smooth manufacturing, with an average annual salary of 4 to 5 lakhs. An ASIC Engineer finds and understands system complexities to devise solutions that enhance system performance, earning an average of 20 lakhs. An Embedded Engineer designs and implements the software used by embedded devices and systems, actively participating in the software development life cycle, earning around 16 lakhs. A Network Support Engineer ensures that internal and external communication systems run smoothly without bugs, with a salary of 3 to 4 lakhs. A Software Engineer identifies the need for new software programs to ease work in various sectors, designing, developing, and improving existing programs, and ensuring proper hardware and software functionality, earning between 4 to 12 lakhs.

Additionally, a Quality Analyst ensures that the development and planning of various test and process plans run smoothly, with an average salary of 4.5 lakhs. A Technician takes part in the initial phases of the software development life cycle, identifying and eliminating potential threats, earning 2 to 2.5 lakhs. The Chief Technical Officer oversees the technical sector of an organization at a managerial level, aligning them with the company's overall growth targets, earning an average of 18 lakhs. An ECE Engineering Consultant acts as a bridge between the client and the working team to ensure client needs are met according to industry regulations, earning around 20 lakhs. Finally, a Data Analyst analyzes raw data from different sectors of a company to derive meaningful results for decision-making, ensuring profitable solutions, and earning between 5 to 8 lakhs.

### Employment Forecast in Advanced Communication Technology in India (2025 - 2030)
The field of Advanced Communication Technology in India is experiencing rapid growth, driven by innovations in 5G and 6G, the Internet of Things, satellite communications, and wireless technologies. 

### Key Industry Drivers
The deployment of 5G and preparations for 6G will lead to significant hiring in network planning, radio frequency design, and protocol development, along with growth in telecom infrastructure, network security, wireless communication, and millimeter-wave technology. The expanding space industry, including ISRO and private satellite companies, will generate demand for satellite communication engineers focusing on satellite system design, communications payloads, and ground station operations. The explosion of connected devices for smart cities and industrial IoT will require professionals skilled in low-power communication protocols, sensor networks, embedded systems, and edge computing. The demand for high-speed internet will create job openings in wireless broadband, Wi-Fi 6, and optical fiber communication, focusing on millimeter-wave systems, software-defined radio, and advanced modulation techniques. Furthermore, increased investment in research and development for next-generation communication technologies, such as optical wireless and quantum communication, will create positions for research engineers and technology specialists.

### Sector-Wise Job Growth Projections and Opportunities
The Telecom sector for 5G and 6G is projected to grow by 10 to 12 percent per year, hiring in RF engineering, network design, and protocol testing. Satellite Communications will see a growth rate of 12 to 15 percent, focusing on satellite payload design and ground station operations. The IoT and Embedded Systems sector is expected to grow by 15 to 18 percent, hiring for IoT communication protocols, sensor networks, and edge computing. Broadband and Wireless communications are projected to grow by 8 to 10 percent, creating jobs in millimeter-wave systems, optical fiber, and Wi-Fi technologies. The Research and Development sector for next-generation communications will see a 10 to 14 percent growth rate, seeking experts in quantum communication, optical wireless, and 6G technologies.

Roles such as Telecom Engineer, Satellite Communication Engineer, IoT Network Engineer, and Network Security Engineer will experience high to very high job growth. These roles require skills in RF design, antenna design, millimeter-wave technologies, network optimization, low-power protocols, cybersecurity, and encryption. Research Engineers for 6G and Quantum Communications, as well as RF System Engineers, will also see high demand, requiring expertise in quantum computing, advanced wireless systems, signal processing, and microwave engineering.

### Key Government Initiatives and Policy Impacts
Several government initiatives impact the industry. The National Digital Communications Policy of 2018 aims to position India as a global leader in communication technologies, attracting investment in 5G and beyond. The Space Policy promotes private-sector participation in satellite communications. The Smart Cities Mission generates demand for IoT, broadband, and wireless communication infrastructure. Finally, the Production Linked Incentive scheme boosts the manufacturing of telecom equipment and network components in India, leading to significant job creation in the sector.

### Skills and Certifications Demand in Industry
Professionals need expertise in 5G and 6G, with certifications from 3GPP, IEEE, and Cisco. Knowledge of IoT and embedded systems, including Arduino, Raspberry Pi, STM32, and LoRaWAN, is essential. Experience with satellite communications equipment and ground stations is highly sought after. Familiarity with wireless protocols such as Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth, LoRa, and NB-IoT is necessary. Additionally, knowledge of Software-Defined Networking and Network Function Virtualization is in high demand.

# Electronics Engineering with Specialization in VLSI Design and Technology

## 1. Overview
The B.Tech in Electronics Engineering with Specialization in VLSI Design and Technology addresses the exponential demand for integrated chips and sensors driven by the proliferation of the digital economy and consumer electronics. Meeting this burgeoning domestic demand is challenging as India currently imports integrated chips in billions of US dollars. The post-COVID global semiconductor market has grown exponentially and is expected to reach one trillion dollars by 2030, driven by technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Electric Vehicles, 5G Networks, the Internet of Things, and Health Care. Realization of these technologies depends on the production of silicon chips, leading to the establishment of many chip-making industries in research and development, design, manufacturing, and testing to fill the gap in the chip supply chain. Overall semiconductor import has surpassed that of gold, standing second only to crude oil, and the deficit is expected to rise further from a long-term economic perspective. Hence, the existing gap must be bridged by realizing indigenous manufacturing of integrated chips.

Most of the tape-out is currently being siliconized in foreign countries since India has only a single Integrated Design to Manufacturing pilot line at the Semi-Conductor Laboratory based on the 180nm Node. Recently, the Government of India has given impetus to the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing policy for full-flow custom design solutions. Foundries and companies are encouraged to set up chip manufacturing units under the Indian Semiconductor Mission to build vibrant ecosystems of semiconductor and display systems. A common concern associated with setting up and running a commercial fab in India is the availability of trained manpower required to run the system. 

A serious crunch is observed in the trained manpower in every aspect of the semiconductor ecosystem in the country. Various schemes and policies are framed by the Government of India to encourage start-ups, MSMEs, industries, and large business houses, including the Chips to Startup programme of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. It is estimated that the total manpower requirement over the next five to seven years will be around 85,000 across undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral levels in the fields of VLSI Technology, Semiconductor Manufacturing, Electronics, Electrical, Mechanical, and Chemical Engineering. The Government of India announced a Semiconductor scheme with a massive outlay to fulfill the Aatma Nirbhar Bharath vision and contribute significantly to the global semiconductor market.

**MSAJCE** is dedicated to becoming a part of this endeavor to create the human resources required for the semiconductor industry in the upcoming years by providing trained engineers through the National Semiconductor Mission. The outcome of this program is to improve the world through transformative education and impactful research by producing outstanding graduates who are knowledgeable, creative, and passionate about building a vibrant semiconductor and display ecosystem to enable India’s emergence as a global hub for electronics manufacturing and design.

B.Tech in Electronics Engineering with Specialization in VLSI Design and Technology is offered in the Faculty of Electronics and Communication Engineering. VLSI is the process of designing and manufacturing integrated circuits. The VLSI design curriculum emphasizes the key aspects of software and hardware design and development of VLSI applications such as device modeling, RF circuit design, testing and diagnosis of VLSI circuits, VLSI signal processing, chip packaging, system design verification, and system on chip. VLSI Design and its applications are found in areas like signal processing, image processing, networks and communication applications, space applications, and quantum computing. This programme aims to cater to the exponential rise in demand for a semiconductor talent pool in India and across the globe, preparing market-ready engineers for the semiconductor technology and electronics industries.

The course is structured in line with the AICTE model curriculum and covers a range of topics from semiconductor device fundamentals, analog and digital circuits to VLSI circuits and design, IC design and technology, semiconductor equipment operation, manufacturing, assembly, testing and packaging, microcontrollers, embedded systems, algorithms in design automation, logic synthesis, testability, device and process simulation, and physical verification flows. It also includes the study and usage of Electronic Design Automation tools and programming and scripting languages for semiconductor design, synthesis, simulation, fabrication, and testing. The main objective of providing this course is to offer varying roles of employment featuring attractive salary incentives and solid professional growth, especially with the establishment of India’s largest semiconductor fab plant at Mysuru. It also prepares students to pursue higher education in reputed universities in India and abroad, as VLSI is in great demand in companies like Intel, IBM, Cadence, Synopsis, and Mentor Graphics. Furthermore, it provides insights into market trends and wider opportunities to take up projects under the Make in India and Digital India schemes, encouraging entrepreneurial endeavors in creating innovative products based on VLSI chipsets.

## 2. Career Prospects
There are numerous job opportunities for VLSI engineers in the Semiconductor industry. These opportunities include roles as Design Engineers, Verification Engineers, CAD Engineers, Application Engineers, Analog Circuit Designers, DFT Engineers, FPGA Verification Engineers, EDA Tool Validation Engineers, and VLSI Micro-architecture Engineers among many others. On successful completion of the course, graduates are recruited in Fabless design companies, Display Fabs, Semiconductor Fabs, Fabs for Compound Semiconductors, Silicon Photonics, Sensors, Discrete Semiconductors, and Semiconductor Assembly, Testing, Marking, and Packaging facilities. Skills in RF circuit design, signal processing, low-power design, and hardware design for AI accelerators are also crucial.

The Production-Linked Incentive scheme aims to increase domestic manufacturing and assembly of electronics, fostering job creation. The shift toward Electric Vehicles and ADAS increases the need for VLSI design in power electronics and control systems.

### Employment Forecast Summary
VLSI Design in India will experience exceptional annual growth in the next five years, fueled by demand in semiconductor manufacturing, telecommunications, IoT, automotive, and AI hardware sectors. The focus on domestic semiconductor fabrication, 5G and 6G networks, AI chip design, and electric vehicle electronics will open up numerous roles for VLSI engineers, especially those with expertise in RF, analog and mixed-signal design, embedded systems, and verification.

As India’s e-commerce market grows, there will be an increasing demand for professionals skilled in data analytics, customer experience design, and supply chain management. In healthcare, as systems embrace digital health, telemedicine, and AI for diagnostics, professionals with expertise in both business systems and IT will be in high demand. Lastly, the smart manufacturing revolution driven by the Internet of Things, AI, and cloud computing will create roles focused on integrating IT systems with industrial processes.
