# Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat

## 1. Initiative Overview
Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat is an initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance unity in diversity across the nation. The initiative was launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the Rashtriya Ekta Divas held on October 31st, 2015, to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The primary goal is to establish a sustained and structured cultural connection among denizens of different regions of India. India is a unique nation whose fabric has been woven by diverse linguistic, cultural, and religious threads, held together into a composite national identity by a rich history of cultural evolution. The program aims to enhance interaction and promote mutual understanding between people of different states and union territories through the concept of state pairing. The paired states carry out activities to promote a sustained and structured cultural connection in areas such as language learning, culture, traditions, music, tourism, cuisine, sports, and the sharing of best practices. Under this initiative, Tamil Nadu is paired with Jammu and Kashmir. 

## 2. College Participation
Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering in Chennai has actively participated in this initiative by conducting two major programs in collaboration with SSM College of Engineering in Parihaspora, Pattan, Baramulla, Jammu and Kashmir. The first activity was a Cultural Exchange Program organized under Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat and Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, with further details accessible through the official Ek Bharat portal. The second activity focused on exploring the winter iconic destination of Gulmarg, Kashmir, alongside the traditional art of Kashmiri carpet weaving, with the presentation material available via a shared Google Drive link.

# Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC)

## 1. Overview
In pursuance of the National Action Plan of the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), Bangalore, for performance evaluation, assessment and accreditation and quality up gradation of institutions of higher education, the NAAC proposes that every accredited institution should establish an Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) as a post-accreditation quality sustenance measure. Since quality enhancement is a continuous process, the IQAC will become a part of an institution’s system and work towards realizing the goals of quality enhancement and sustenance. The prime task of the IQAC is to develop a system for conscious, consistent and catalytic improvement in the performance of institutions. The IQAC will make a significant and meaningful contribution in the post-accreditation phase of institutions. During the post-accreditation period, the IQAC will channelise the efforts and measures of an institution towards academic excellence.

The guidelines provided will facilitate **MSAJCE** in the creation and operation of the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC). The work of the IQAC is the first step towards the internalization and institutionalization of quality enhancement. Its success depends upon the sense of belongingness and participation it can inculcate in all the constituents of **MSAJCE**. It will not be yet another hierarchical structure or recordkeeping exercise in **MSAJCE**, rather it will be a facilitative and participative voluntary system of **MSAJCE**. The IQAC has the potential to become a vehicle for ushering in quality by working out intervention strategies to remove deficiencies and enhance quality. Quality circles in industries operate on similar lines.

## 2. Objective of IQAC
The primary objective is to develop a system for conscious, consistent and catalytic action to improve the academic and administrative performance of **MSAJCE**. It also aims to promote measures for the institutional functioning towards quality enhancement through internalization of quality culture and institutionalization of best practices.

## 3. Strategies
The IQAC shall evolve mechanisms and procedures for ensuring timely, efficient and progressive performance of academic, administrative and financial tasks. It will focus on the relevance and quality of academic and research programmes, as well as equitable access to and affordability of academic programmes for various sections of society. The IQAC is responsible for the optimization and integration of modern methods of teaching and learning, the credibility of evaluation procedures, and ensuring the adequacy, maintenance and functioning of the support structure and services. It also focuses on research sharing and networking with other institutions in India and abroad.

## 4. Functions
The functions include the development and application of quality benchmarks for the various academic and administrative activities of **MSAJCE**, and the dissemination of information on the various quality parameters of higher education. The IQAC is responsible for the organization of workshops and seminars on quality related themes and the promotion of quality circles. It takes charge of the documentation of the various programmes and activities leading to quality improvement, acting as a nodal agency of **MSAJCE** for quality-related activities, and the preparation of the Annual Quality Assurance Report (AQAR) to be submitted to NAAC based on the quality parameters.

## 5. Benefits
The IQAC will facilitate a heightened level of clarity and focus in institutional functioning towards quality enhancement and facilitate internalization of the quality culture for NAAC for Quality and Excellence in Higher Education. It contributes to the enhancement and integration among the various activities of **MSAJCE** and institutionalizes many good practices. The cell provides a sound basis for decision making to improve institutional functioning, acts as a change agent in **MSAJCE**, and leads to better internal communication.

## 6. The Role of Coordinator
The role of the coordinator of the IQAC is crucial in ensuring the effective functioning of all the members. The coordinator of the IQAC may be a senior person with expertise in quality aspects. The coordinator may be a full-time functionary or a senior academic entrusted with the IQAC as an additional responsibility. Secretarial assistance may be facilitated by the administration. It is preferable that the coordinator may have a sound knowledge about computers, various functions, and usage for effective communication.

## 7. Operational Features of the IQAC
Quality assurance is a by-product of ongoing efforts to define the objectives of an institution, to have a work plan to achieve them and to specify the checks and balances to evaluate the degree to which each of the tasks is fulfilled. Hence devotion and commitment to improvement rather than mere institutional control is the basis for devising procedures and instruments for assuring quality. The right balance between the health and growth of an institution needs to be struck. The IQAC has to ensure that whatever is done in **MSAJCE** for education is done efficiently and effectively with high standards. In order to do this, the IQAC will have to first establish procedures and modalities to collect data and information on various aspects of institutional functioning. The coordinators of the IQAC and the secretary have a major role in implementing these functions. The IQAC may derive major support from the already existing units and mechanisms that contribute to the listed functions. The operational features and functions discussed are broad based to facilitate institutions towards academic excellence and institutions may adapt them to their specific needs.

# Kaushal Augmentation and Restructuring Mission of AICTE (KARMA)

## 1. Overview and Objectives
The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) is initiating the Kaushal Augmentation and Restructuring Mission of AICTE (KARMA) for all AICTE-approved institutions in the country. The initiative aims to overcome the dual challenge of the scarcity of skilled manpower in jobs and the low skill level of those who are presently employed. The scheme focuses on strategically planned skill initiatives to create a skilled and certified workforce that not only contributes towards the growth of India but also drives the country into becoming the global skills capital. It encourages institutions to make the best use of the available higher education infrastructure during off-hours for skill training. This is achieved by realigning the existing infrastructure, training aids, syllabi, and curricula as per National Skills Qualifications Framework aligned qualifications. The scheme is applicable to candidates who have passed at least the tenth standard or completed ITI courses. The training provided under the scheme focuses on domain-specific, demand-led skill training activities, preferably in core engineering sectors, leading directly to employment.

## 2. Skilling Models
The AICTE has proposed three models for the skilling of in-school students, school dropouts, and students pursuing technical education. Model 1 targets school dropouts after they have passed class ten, including both recent and long-term dropouts. Model 2 targets advanced-level skilling for students already studying in AICTE-approved technical institutions. It introduces a skill up-gradation program for present technical students to make them industry-ready by offering advanced skilling courses during their fourth to seventh semesters, with assessments similar to the standard KARMA criteria. Model 3 integrates school education with higher education to skill students, acknowledging that education needs to shift from being corrective to connective and from transactional to relational. To establish this connection, AICTE suggests that higher education institutions start offering skill-based training for nearby school students once a week using a hub-and-spoke model.

## 3. College Implementation and Approvals
Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering has been approved by AICTE to conduct courses under the KARMA initiative. Under Model 1, the institute was approved to conduct two courses, each with an approved intake of thirty students. These courses are Computer Hardware Network Maintenance and Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Technician. The official approval letter for Model 1 can be accessed via the AICTE facilities portal. Under Model 2, **MSAJCE** was approved to conduct five courses. These include the AI and Machine Learning Developer course, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Technician, Additive Manufacturing Technician focusing on 3D printing, a Certificate Course in Embedded System Design using ARM Cortex Microcontrollers, and Architectural Drafting and Basic 3D Design using Autodesk Revit. The institute has registered these five courses, and they are currently in progress. The official approval letter for Model 2, as well as the detailed course registration information, are also publicly accessible through the AICTE facilities portal.

# Sathak Innovation and Incubation Foundation

## 1. Overview
The main objects to be pursued by the company upon its incorporation are to promote commerce, science, education and research by helping, establishing and incubating startups, individuals, teams with innovative ideas to make prototypes and to convert them into Products. Another objective is to promote a culture of innovation driven entrepreneurship in the fields of science, engineering, technology, commerce, agriculture, health care, medicine, pharmacy, education, arts, sports and other various fields. Furthermore, it aims to establish, help establish and or manage infrastructure, laboratories, to make and test prototypes or products, pilot plant production facilities, software development facilities, training and human resource development centre, propogate new scientific and technologies development and innovation from idea stage to full scale commercial production or any part of this chain. For the above purposes to assist, co-operate or collaborates with any establishment, laboratory, technology business incubators centre, organisation or institution in India or abroad.

## 2. Incubation Cell
Various programs and initiatives to support aspiring entrepreneurs and early-stage startups are provided. Incubation services typically include 5000 square feet physical office space, several 100, 400, 700 seater halls for conducting many events in Entrepreneurship, infrastructure, and shared resources for startups. There are funding opportunities to startups through grants, seed funding, or connections to potential investors. Mentorship programs where experienced professionals and industry experts provide guidance and support to entrepreneurs and startups are available. There is access to a network of investors, venture capitalists, and angel investors who are interested in supporting innovative ideas and startups. The cell organizes events, workshops, and training programs to foster innovation, entrepreneurial skills, and knowledge sharing. It also facilitates partnerships with academic institutions, industry bodies, and government agencies to create synergies and opportunities for startups. The Incubation Lead is Akshita K at SIIF, **MSAJCE**, Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering in Chennai 603103. She can be contacted at info@siif.ventures or through www.siif.ventures.

## 3. National Innovation and Startup Policy
The Vision is to cater the needs of student entrepreneurs with innovative ideas there by introducing a culture of entrepreneurship inside campus which will strengthen our education system and there by promoting the national economic and social growth. The Mission is to develop an ecosystem with required infrastructure that can enable students and faculty to innovate and prototype their potential ideas with industrial standards and support from Government, industry and reputed academic institutions around the world and help them to realize their potentials.

## 4. Objectives
The Short Term Objectives include helping student groups to prototype their ideas, improving innovation, creative and design thinking among student community, and providing incubation facility for faculty driven start-ups and student or Alumni start-ups. Other short term objectives are to organize FDP, seminars and workshops, distinguish talks for students, Faculty and Alumni and promote entrepreneurial culture, and to strengthen institute industry interaction cell activity and effectively use the outcomes for achieving the mission. The Long Term Objectives are to associate with DST, CII, MSME and other academic institutions for transferring world class facility for **MSAJCE** IEDC activities, and to improve quality of research work among students and to attain patent, which can be commercially used in production. Further long term objectives are to provide a platform for students to develop innovative products with global recognition and generate business opportunities, generate revenues through consultancy work and student start-ups, and spread awareness to students and faculty regarding IPR related activities.

## 5. Strategic Partnership Linkage
**MSAJCE** has strategic partnership linkage with Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India (EDII) in Chennai. Another linkage is with the National Innovation Foundation (NIF) of India to submit ideas and apply for schemes. **MSAJCE** also procures fund from AICTE for the Entrepreneurship Development Cell.

## 6. Committee Members
Dr. K.S. Srinivasan <!--ent_038--> (Principal), Principal of Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering (**MSAJCE**) in Chennai, serves as the President. Mr. Prakadesh Subramanian <!--ent_282-->, Strategic Partner at SIIF in Chennai, serves as the Incubation Coordinator. Mr. Parvez Aalam <!--ent_278-->, CEO of Crescent Innovation Incubation Council in Chennai, also serves as an Incubation Coordinator. Mr. Thiyagaraja Gupta <!--ent_375-->, Deputy Controller of Patents and Designs, is the Patent Expert. Ahamed Jamel, AMT IT consultant at 4A technology, serves as an Alumni Entrepreneur. Abdur Rahim Salih, Director and CEO of V5 Innovations Pvt Ltd, is another Alumni Entrepreneur. Asim Ali L, CMO at Customer Labs, also serves as an Alumni Entrepreneur.

## 7. Thrust Area
The plans for thrust areas include developing Strategies and governance for Promoting Innovation Entrepreneurship in the institute, and Creating Innovation Pipeline and Pathways for Entrepreneurs and Startups. Other plans are Building Organizational Capacity, Human Resources and Incentive, along with Collaboration, Co-creation, Business Relationship and knowledge Exchange. Furthermore, the plans cover Incubation and Pre-Incubation support at SIIF, IP Ownership Rights for Technologies Developed at **MSAJCE** and SIIF, Pedagogy and Learning Interventions for Supporting Innovations and Start-ups, and Entrepreneurial Performance Impact Assessment.

## 8. KPI Monitor & Evaluation
The Key Performance Indicators for the Vision are an increase in Self-Employment Rate, 5 Established Start-ups per year, and NIRF Rankings. The Goal is to establish the Environment with multiple level of support for innovation, Entrepreneurship and startups, where students will choose Entrepreneurship as a career, which is monitored by ARIIA Rankings. The Outcomes include all student and faculty having entrepreneurship orientation, and being motivated to start any entrepreneurial activity, aiming for 5 IPR or Innovations developed ideas per year, and 5 Student or Early-Stage Start-ups to be formed per year. Other outcomes are having an in-house Expert Capacity facility available for Advisory Services, exposing 25 percent of Student and faculty mass to awareness or orientation building programs, and covering students through entrepreneurship Education like MOOC, Class Room, and Experiential Learning programs. Additionally, the outcomes expect 250 beneficiaries accessing the infrastructure and facilities per day, month and Year, 25 percent innovators identified with 25 awarded or recognized and 25 supported. It is aimed that 5 percent of Student projects turn to commercialize Innovations, 5 IPR based products or services are generated and registration filed, an in-house trained professional is developed for advisory services, 5 Research Studies on Entrepreneurship are published, and 2 Regional, National and International linkages are established for the start-up and innovation. Finally, 5 percent Representatives of experts and entrepreneurial students across Departments and Disciplines are targeted, along with 5 Beneficiaries Referred to Incubators or investors for further support through Start-up Cell, and 10 Beneficiaries generated under various schemes and programs leveraged and converged at Start-up Cell. These are verified through Quarterly News Letter, Biannual Survey, and Monthly progress report. The Activities include 5 Education or Skill certification programs on Entrepreneurship, IIPR, Innovation, 25 workshops, awareness, and market outreach events, orientation, advocacy meetings, and 12 networking events organized. They also include 5 skill and competency development training programs, FDPs or EDPs organized, 5 research studies related to Entrepreneurship conducted, 1 national and regional award and campus Hackathon like events organized, incentivizing Entrepreneurship and Innovation with services and facilities like Start-up Manual, policies, tool kits, and 1 percent of total budget per year spent against total institution revenue for start-up, along with Budget allocation and Spend ratio for the start-up mandate in the institute. These are verified by Biannual Survey, Quarterly News Letter, Monthly progress report, and Review Meetings.

## 9. Tentative plan for the next 5 years
The tentative plan for the next five years includes conducting a One Day Workshop on Entrepreneurship and Innovation as Career Opportunity once a year. A One Day Workshop on Problem Solving, Design Thinking, Ideation Workshop or Campus Hackathon will be conducted once a year. A Field or Exposure Visit to Village, Society, School, Industry, or Market to identity real Life Problem will be conducted once a year. A National Conference or workshop on Start-up, Social Innovation and Entrepreneurship will be conducted once a year. A Demo Day acting as an Exhibition Cum Demo for PoCs and Mentorship Session for Innovators or Student Entrepreneurs will be held twice a year. Internships at Innovation and Start-up Centre, Startups, or Incubation Units during Semester Break will be facilitated once a year. A Boot camp for Innovation product development will be held once a year. Innovation Day Celebrations will occur once a year. National Science Day will be celebrated once a year. A Workshop on Funding Opportunities for Innovation and Entrepreneurship Development will be held once a year. SATHAKATHON, a National Level 24 hours Hackathon, will be held once a year. A Short Term Training course on Innovation, Start-up and Entrepreneurship will be conducted once a year.

## 10. Entrepreneurship Development Cell
The roles and responsibilities include encouraging the students to become entrepreneurs by organizing entrepreneurship development programs and making them participate in the activities organized by the external agencies. It also organizes the training for Startup or Incubator and arranges the mentoring to proceed further. Furthermore, it coordinates with the Strategy partner of Sathak Innovation Incubation Cell (SIIF) and executes various Activities. The team includes Mr. S.V. Vinodh <!--ent_318--> from EEE as Head of EDC and HEC, Mrs. N. Kavitha <!--ent_418--> from MBA, Mr. Ajin Sijo John <!--ent_119--> from MECH, and Mrs. N. Selvi <!--ent_420--> for Training.

## 11. Institution Innovation Council (IIC-**MSAJCE**)
**MSAJCE** Innovation Council (IIC-**MSAJCE**) had been constituted in **MSAJCE** as per the guidelines of the Ministry of Human Resource Development Innovation Cell (MIC). The Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), Government of India has established MHRD's Innovation Cell (MIC) to systematically foster the culture of Innovation amongst all Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). The primary mandate of MIC is to encourage, inspire and nurture young students by supporting them to work with new ideas and transform them into prototypes while they are in their formative years. MIC has envisioned encouraging the creation of Institution's Innovation Council (IICs) across selected HEIs. A network of these IICs will be established to promote innovation in **MSAJCE** through multitudinous modes leading to an innovation promotion eco-system in the campuses. The major focus of IIC is to create a vibrant local innovation ecosystem, and to support the Start-up Mechanism in HEIs. It aims to prepare the institute for Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements Framework, establish Function at Ecosystem for Scouting Ideas and Pre-incubation of Ideas, and develop better Cognitive Ability for Technology Students.

## 12. Functions of IICs
The functions include conducting various innovation and entrepreneurship-related activities prescribed by the ministry of Education's Innovation cell as and when announced by it. It will identify and reward innovations and share success stories. It will also organize periodic workshops, seminars, and interactions with entrepreneurs, investors, professionals and create a mentor pool for student innovators. Furthermore, it will network with peers and national entrepreneurship development organizations, create an Institution's Innovation portal to highlight innovative projects carried out by **MSAJCE**'s faculty and students, and organize Hackathons, idea competitions, and mini-challenges with the involvement of industries.

## 13. Vision and Mission
The Vision is to be a centre of excellence for transforming students into proficient Electrical and Electronics Engineers through sustainable practices. The Mission includes imparting core fundamental knowledge and necessary skills in Electrical and Electronics Engineering through innovative teaching and learning methodology. It also inculcates critical thinking, ethics, lifelong learning and creativity needed for industry and society. It aims to cultivate the students with all-round competencies for career, higher education and self-employability.

Information technology helps the business world to view changes in the global markets faster than they usually do. Due to the development of this technology, globalization has increased and the world is brought closer. Information is stored and shared quickly and easily across the globe. The 12 Programme Outcomes (POs) for the B.Tech IT programme at MSAJCE defining graduate competencies.

Programme Outcomes (PO) — B.Tech Information Technology, MSAJCE

PO1 — Engineering Knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2 — Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3 — Design/Development Of Solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

PO4 — Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

PO5 — Modern Tool Usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

PO6 — The Engineer and Society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

PO7 — Environment and Sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.

PO8 — Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

PO9 — Individual and Team Work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multi disciplinary settings.

PO10 — Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large.

PO11 — Project Management and Finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one's own work.

PO12 — Life-long Learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

The Information Technology (IT) industry in India is poised for strong growth over the next five years, driven by domestic and global trends.

Key Drivers of IT Growth:

1. **Digital Transformation:** Businesses across all sectors are adopting Cloud computing, AI, Big Data, IoT, and Blockchain. Demand for cloud engineers, data scientists, AI specialists, and DevOps engineers will rise.
2. **Cloud Computing:** Cloud market in India is growing rapidly. AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud will create high demand for cloud architects, cloud administrators, and cloud security specialists. Hybrid cloud solutions will generate opportunities in cloud migration, cloud operations, and cloud infrastructure management.
3. **Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning:** AI is transforming healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and retail. By 2030, demand will rise for data scientists, AI researchers, machine learning engineers, and AI-enabled software developers. Skills needed: AI ethics, deep learning, AI model deployment.
4. **Cyber Security:** With increasing cyberattacks and regulations (GDPR, Personal Data Protection Bill), demand for cybersecurity experts will grow. Roles: ethical hackers, incident response professionals, security architects, SOC analysts.
5. **Fintech and Blockchain:** India's cashless economy push requires blockchain developers, smart contract auditors, and DeFi specialists.
6. **5G and Telecommunications:** Rollout of 5G will create demand for 5G network engineers, telecommunications architects, and telecom software developers. IoT will see a boom in smart cities, agriculture, and healthcare.
7. **E-Governance and Smart Cities:** Government initiatives like Digital India, Smart Cities Mission, and Make in India will create roles for IT project managers, data engineers, IoT developers, and cloud solutions architects.
8. **Outsourcing and Off-shoring:** India will continue as a global IT outsourcing hub with demand for application developers, IT consultants, systems integrators, and support specialists.

# **MSAJCE** — About

## 1. Overview
The Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering (**MSAJCE**), established on 5th July 2001 under the aegis of Mohamed Sathak Trust, is approved by AICTE New Delhi, and is affiliated to Anna University Chennai and the Government of Tamil Nadu. **MSAJCE** strives to continuously upgrade its facilities to provide quality technical education to meet industrial and societal needs by providing skill-based training with state-of-the-art facilities.

**MSAJCE** campus sprawls over 70 acres of greenery located inside the SIPCOT IT Park in Siruseri, and it is surrounded by multinational IT companies such as TCS, CTS, Intellect, Aspire, Steria, Polaris, and FSS. **MSAJCE** has good infrastructure facilities such as spacious classrooms, drawing halls, laboratories, seminar halls, computer facilities with internet and wifi connectivity, a library, workshops, an auditorium, and a playground. **MSAJCE** is well connected by road, rail, and air from various parts of the country. A team of well-qualified and experienced faculty supports the teaching and learning process. **MSAJCE** provides equal importance for academic, co-curricular, and extracurricular activities. **MSAJCE** provides all kinds of training for the professional and overall transformation of the students.

## 2. Why Join **MSAJCE**
**MSAJCE** is located in a green, lush environment at the Siruseri IT Park, surrounded by over a hundred leading IT industries like TCS, CTS, Infosys, Intellect, FSS, and HCL. It offers state-of-the-art facilities with industry-collaborative technology centers. A qualified, experienced, and dedicated team of faculty members supports the students, while a well-defined academic process ensures smart learning. Students are involved in various research and industrial projects, industrial hackathons, and project competitions that help them gain competency-based learning. Professional societies, club activities, and student chapter activities enable innovative learning. A student exchange program is also available for cultural learning. 

Furthermore, **MSAJCE** provides internships, industrial visits, guest lectures, and seminars or webinars by industrial experts to meet industrial expectations. **MSAJCE** features a communication language learning facility that offers training in English, German, and Japanese. Value-added courses and technology training are provided to bridge the gap between the institute and the industry. **MSAJCE** boasts a good placement record and provides robust support for higher education, helping students to become successful entrepreneurs.

## 3. Campus Location & Google Maps
Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering is located at:
34, Rajiv Gandhi Salai (OMR), Inside SIPCOT IT Park, Siruseri, Egattur, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 603103, India.

The college is situated within the Siruseri IT Park, making it easily accessible via the Old Mahabalipuram Road. Its precise coordinates are approximately **12°50'08.9"N 80°13'07.0"E**
Plus Code: **R6P9+8C Egattur, Tamil Nadu**.

Official Map Directions Link: [Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering on Google Maps](https://maps.app.goo.gl/nrTgXSwx1h76SjdSA)

## 4. Local Essential Services, Emergency Facilities & Government Offices

### 🚓 Police & Security
- **Kelambakkam Police Station**: The primary jurisdiction for the IT Park; CCTV feeds from the park are linked here. Located approximately 4–5 km away.
- **Thazhambur Police Station**: A closer outpost for the Navalur/Thazhambur stretch, often handling immediate patrolling for the southern entry of the park.
- **Internal Security**: The park operates a dedicated **24/7 mobile patrol SUV** with a direct emergency contact number for employees, supplemented by extensive CCTV coverage managed by SIPCOT.

### 🚒 Fire & Rescue
- **SIPCOT Industrial Fire Station**: Located **inside** the IT Park on First Cross Road. This is the primary response unit for fire emergencies within the campus. (Contact: 044-27470720 / 044-24401213)
- **Tamil Nadu Fire & Rescue Services (Siruseri Unit)**: Co-located with the SIPCOT station, equipped for industrial and high-rise rescue operations.

### 🏥 Hospitals & Medical Care
- **Dr. Kamakshi Memorial Hospital**: Located directly **opposite the SIPCOT gate** on OMR. This is the nearest major multi-specialty private hospital for emergencies.
- **Punarjeevan Hospital**: Located approximately **2.2 km** away in the Siruseri/Navalur area.
- **Supreme Speciality Hospitals** & **Marhura Hospital**: Nearby private facilities in the immediate vicinity.
- **Iswarya Hospital**: A large NABH-accredited multi-specialty hospital located about **8 km** away in Kottivakkam (towards the city), offering advanced trauma and specialty care.
- **Government Hospital**: The nearest government facility is the **Primary Health Centre (PHC) in Kelambakkam** or **Thazhambur**, roughly 4–6 km away. For major government trauma care, the **Government Hospital in Tambaram** (approx. 15 km) is the referral center.

### 🏛️ Other Government Offices
- **SIPCOT IT Park Project Office**: Located within the complex for administrative and infrastructure issues.
- **Regional Transport Office (RTO)**: The nearest RTO is in **Sholinganallur** (approx. 6 km away) for vehicle registration and license services.
- **Post Offices**:
 - **Navalur Branch Post Office (B.O)**: Serves the 600130 pin code area (closest to the park entrance).
 - **Thazhambur Sub Post Office (S.O)**: The main sorting office for the region.
 - **Kelambakkam Post Office**: Located ~7 km away.
- **Aadhar/Seva Centers**: Several private CSC (Common Service Centers) operate in **Navalur** and **Thazhambur** villages for Aadhar, PAN, and utility bill payments.

## 5. History, Lifestyle & Future Developments in Siruseri

### 🏛️ History & Significance
- **Scale**: Spanning approximately **782–800 acres**, it is the **second-largest IT park in Asia** and the largest in South India.
- **SEZ Status**: Designated as a **Special Economic Zone (SEZ)** in August 2006, offering tax incentives and streamlined regulations for exporters.
- **Evolution**: Developed by **SIPCOT** (State Industries Promotion Corporation of Tamil Nadu) starting in the early 2000s to decongest Chennai’s city center and create a dedicated "Cyber City" along the Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR).
- **Recent Milestones**: In 2022, a **₹48 crore Trade Facilitation Center** was inaugurated to support exporters. The park recently transitioned into a hub for **AI and Cloud infrastructure** with massive data center investments in 2025.

### 🚇 Upcoming Infrastructure (2026–2028)
- **Chennai Metro Phase II**: The **Purple Line (Corridor 3: Madhavaram–SIPCOT)** and **Corridor 5** are under construction. The **Siruseri SIPCOT Metro Station** is expected to be operational by **late 2026 to 2028**, directly connecting the park to central Chennai and reducing commute times significantly.
- **Road Upgrades**: An **under-pass at Potheri Junction** and extensions to the **Outer Ring Road (ORR)** are planned to decongest the NH-45 and OMR intersection, improving access to the airport and Chengalpattu.
- **Campus Expansions**: Major firms like **HCL** and **L&T** have announced plans for adjacent expansions in 2026, adding further office capacity.

### 🏘️ Residential & Cost of Living
Siruseri has evolved from a remote work hub into a thriving residential suburb:
- **Property Rates**: As of 2026, the average property price is approximately **₹6,400 – ₹6,450 per sq. ft.**, with an annual appreciation of **8–12%**.
- **Rental Market**: High demand from IT professionals drives rentals.
 - **2 BHK**: ₹25,000 – ₹32,000/month.
 - **3 BHK**: ₹30,000 – ₹35,000/month.
 - **Villas**: ₹40,000 – ₹60,000+/month.
- **Key Residential Projects**: New gated communities include **Hiranandani Verona Block**, **Urbando Kosmos Solaris**, **KG Earth Homes**, and **Isha Symphony Villas**.

### 🎡 Nearby Attractions & Lifestyle
Located near the **East Coast Road (ECR)**, Siruseri offers easy access to leisure spots:
- **Recreation**: **VGP Universal Kingdom** (amusement park) and **MGM Dizzee World** are nearby.
- **Culture**: **Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum** (open-air museum of South Indian art/architecture) and **ISKCON Chennai**.
- **Beaches**: **Uthandi Beach**, **Injambakkam Beach**, and **Muttukadu Beach** are within a 10–15 minute drive.
- **Dining & Stay**: The area hosts premium hotels like **Novotel Chennai Sipcot**, **ibis Chennai Sipcot**, and **Regenta Central**, alongside diverse dining options ranging from local messes to fine dining at **The Square**.

### 🎓 Educational & Research Institutions
- **Chennai Mathematical Institute (CMI)**: A premier research institute for mathematics and computer science located adjacent to the IT Park.
- **Schools**: Reputed institutions like **The School (KFI)**, **Padma Adarsh Higher Secondary School**, and **Kidzee** serve the residential community.

## 6. Shopping, Dining, Nightlife & Local Utilities

### 🛍️ Shopping Malls & Retail Hubs
While there are no massive "city-style" malls strictly inside the IT park gates, the immediate surrounding stretches (Egattur, Navalur, Thazhambur) offer extensive retail options:
- **The Marina Mall (Egattur)**: A major 1.5 million sq. ft. lifestyle destination located right at the edge of Siruseri (Egattur, OMR). It features international brands (Marks & Spencer, Levi's), a SPAR supermarket, food court, INOX theater, and Timezone gaming. Open daily 10 AM to 10 PM.
- **Thazhambur High Road Market**: A bustling commercial strip **3 km** away, densely packed with showrooms, clothing brands, electronics stores, and lifestyle outlets.
- **ECR Shopping Complexes**: Towards the East Coast Road (10–15 mins away), you find large format stores like **Decathlon** (sports), **IKEA** (home furnishings, near Thoraipakkam), and **Croma/Reliance Digital**.
- **Local Retail**: Inside the Siruseri/Navalur junction, there are numerous mini-marts, **Reliance Smart Point**, **More Supermarket**, and **Nilgiris** for daily groceries.

### 🎬 Entertainment & Leisure
- **Cinemas**: 
 - **INOX** (inside The Marina Mall, Egattur).
 - **SPI Cinemas** (Palace Heights, Thoraipakkam, approx. 6 km away).
- **Gaming & Bowling**: **Timezone** (The Marina Mall) and bowling arenas at nearby malls (20–25 min drive).

### 🍽️ Dining & Nightlife
Siruseri has a vibrant food scene catering to IT professionals and students:
- **Food Streets**: The **Navalur Junction** and **Thazhambur Main Road** are lined with hundreds of restaurants, ranging from quick-service (McDonald's, KFC, Domino's) to fine dining.
- **Popular Chains**: **Starbucks**, **Barista**, **The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf**, and **Burger King** have multiple outlets in the Navalur/Thazhambur stretch.
- **Local Favorites**: Numerous "mess" style eateries inside the IT park and affordable South Indian tiffin centers (like **A2B** and **Saravana Bhavan**) surround the campus.
- **Nightlife**: Pubs and breweries like **The Park** (hotel bar), **Highway 74**, and **Palm Beach** are located along the ECR and OMR stretch, about 10–15 minutes away.

### 🏦 Banks & ATMs
- **Inside the Park**: Almost every major IT building has an ATM lobby. The SIPCOT administrative block houses branches of **State Bank of India (SBI)**, **HDFC Bank**, and **ICICI Bank**.
- **Outside**: The **Navalur Junction** is a banking hub with 24/7 ATMs and branches of nearly all major Indian and international banks (**Citi**, **Standard Chartered**, **Axis**, **HSBC**).

### 🚗 Fuel & Automotive
- **Fuel Stations**: Multiple high-capacity fuel bunks (IOCL, BPCL, HPCL) with attached convenience stores (**Smart Bazaar**, **In & Out**) are located at the Siruseri entrance, Navalur, and Thazhambur.
- **Service Centers**: Showrooms and service centers for major car and two-wheeler brands (Hyundai, Maruti, Honda, TVS) are clustered along the OMR service road near Navalur.

## 7. Official Emergency Contact Numbers
Here are the official emergency contact numbers specifically for the Siruseri IT Park (SIPCOT) area and its immediate jurisdiction (Kelambakkam/Chengalpattu):

### 🚒 Fire & Rescue (Siruseri IT Park)
The **SIPCOT IT Park Fire Station** is located inside the park premises.
- **Station Phone**: **044-27470720**
- **Mobile (Duty Officer)**: **+91-9445086139** / **+91-9600984344**
- **Location**: First Cross Road, SIPCOT IT Park, Siruseri.
- **Emergency Dial**: **101** (Routes to nearest unit).

### 🚓 Police Station (Jurisdiction: Kelambakkam)
Siruseri falls under the **Kelambakkam Police Station**.
- **Station Phone**: **044-27474274** (Landline)
- **Alternate/Post Phone**: **044-27475230**
- **Location**: Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Kelambakkam (approx. 2-3 km from Siruseri gate).
- **Emergency Dial**: **100**.

### 🏥 Government Hospitals (Nearest to Siruseri)
There is no large government hospital *inside* Siruseri; the nearest government facilities are in Kelambakkam and Chengalpattu.
- **Government Primary Health Centre (PHC), Kelambakkam**:
 - **Phone**: **044-27474700**
 - **Location**: Vandalur-Kelambakkam Road.
- **Government Chengalpattu Medical College Hospital** (Major Trauma/Govt Facility):
 - **Phone**: **044-27426566**
 - **Distance**: ~15 km from Siruseri.
- **Emergency Ambulance**: Dial **108** (Free government ambulance with life support).

### 🏛️ District Administration & Control Rooms (Chengalpattu)
Siruseri is in **Chengalpattu District**.
- **District Collector (Chengalpattu)**: **044-27427412**
- **District Disaster Control Room**: **1077** or **044-27427414**
- **WhatsApp Helpline (Chengalpattu Dist.)**: **+91-9444272345**

raw_markdown:
# Learning Centre (Library)

## 1. Overview
The Library is the Heart of every academic Institution. **MSAJCE** encourages all students and staff members to make the best use of the library that has been carefully built up since the inception of **MSAJCE** as a cardinal support service of the Institute. The prime objective of the library is to provide the right information to the right readers at the right time in the right manner by bibliographic sources and full text sources in the form of print as well as digital in the disciplines of Science, Engineering, Technology, Humanities, Management, and General fields. These are kept in separate places such as the stack section, reference Section, and Periodical Section to support the scholarly and informational needs of the Institute Community. The library is housed in a spacious area of 8978 Square feet covering the Ground Floor and First Floor. It is fully computerized with more than 29853 books and 1885 reference volumes stacked for the benefit of staff and students. The library subscribes to around 35 specialized Printed journals and 20 magazines. It is also a member of DELNET and the J-Gate database is subscribed yearly.

The library regularly features the addition of new titles and volumes in all subject areas. Every effort has been made to acquire all of the titles that the faculty have recommended. Reputable newspapers, weekly, and fortnightly publications are subscribed to so that the students can stay up to date on current events. Bar-coded Technology, open source software called Koha, internet connectivity, and WIFI facility are all available to users.

## 2. Library Resources and Stack Collection Details
The library holds 29853 volumes comprising 5628 titles. There are 1885 reference books and 3790 e-books available. The library subscribes to 35 national journals, 20 magazines, and 5 daily newspapers. There are 106 back volumes, 356 CD-ROMs, and 260 project reports. It provides access to 1379 e-journals through DELNET and 1800 international journals through the Gale Database. 

## 3. Library Working Hours
The library is open from Monday to Saturday from 8:00 A.M. to 7:00 P.M. On all Sundays, it operates from 10:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M.

## 4. Printed Journals
The Mechanical Engineering department, Electronics and Communication Engineering department, and Electrical and Electronics Engineering department each have 6 printed journals. The Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology departments together have 10 printed journals. The Civil Engineering department has 4 printed journals, and the Science and Humanities department has 5 printed journals, bringing the total to 37 printed journals.

## 5. Open Access E-Journals
Various open access e-journals are available. The Directory of Open Access Journals is accessible at http://doaj.org/. BioMed Central can be accessed at http://www.biomedcentral.com/journals. Scientific Research Publishing is available at http://www.scirp.org/. Core is accessible at https://www.core.ac.uk/. Trans stellar journal publication and Research Consultancy can be found at http://www.tiprc.org/. Science Publications is available at http://thescipub.com. Research India Publication is accessible at http://www.ripublication.com/. The International Association of Engineering and Management can be accessed at http://www.iaeme.com/. The Seventh Sense Research Group is available at http://www.internationaljournalssrg.org/. Google Scholar can be accessed at https://www.scholar.google.com. arXis for Scholar Articles is available at https://www.arxiv.org. Hindawi Publishers can be accessed at http://www.hindawi.com/. The CSC Open-Access Library is available at http://www.cscjournals.org/. OMICS International can be found at http://www.omicsonline.org. The Indian Academy of Science is accessible at http://www.ias.ac.in.

## 6. E-Library
The e-library resources include Delnet accessible at https://delnet.in/, and J-Gate at https://jgateplus.com/. The National Digital library is available at https://ndl.iitkgp.ac.in/, while the World digital Library can be accessed at https://www.wdl.org/. Shodhganga is accessible at https://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/, and Shodhsindu at https://ess.inflibnet.ac.in/. NPTEL Videos can be found at http://www.nptelvideos.com/, and NLIST E-Resources are available at https://nlist.inflibnet.ac.in/veresources.php.

## 7. E-books
A wide array of e-book databases is provided. The Directory of open Access Books is at http://www.doabooks.org/, and the E-Books Directory is at http://www.e-booksdirectory.com/. AMS Books are available at http://www.ams.org/, and Intech at http://www.intechopen.com/. Audio Books for free can be accessed at http://www.audiobooksforfree.com/, and New Free Books at https://www.free-ebooks.net/. # Mechanical Engineering (Mech)

## 1. Overview
Mechanical engineering is the oldest and second largest engineering discipline. Mechanical engineering provides a solid foundation for professional engineering practices and is concerned with design, development, manufacture, and operation of many types of plants, machinery and mechanical products. This branch of study develops the students ability to apply scientific principles in the design and analysis of mechanical and energy conversion systems. Students are challenged with design problems in most of the major courses which provide opportunities of developing creativity in solving real world problems. New areas like Robotics, cryogenic engineering, composite materials, Nano materials and technology, Renewable energy resources etc, have tremendous growth in future. At the outset the students will be able to create innovative ideas to find solutions to real world problems with new perspective and good practical skills using science and math concepts. Organising ability, practicing, ability to get on well with people of all types, ability to keep them under pressure and technically to work in a manufacturing area are an asset in the fields.

## 2. Programme
The program offered is a B.E. in Mechanical Engineering. The duration is four years for regular students and three years for lateral entry students, comprising eight and six semesters, respectively. The total intake is 60 seats, divided equally with 30 for the government quota and 30 for the management quota. Eligibility for the program requires completion of the 10+2 system of education, and students must have secured a pass in Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics in their qualifying examination. The curriculum and syllabus follow both the 2021 Regulation and the 2017 Regulation. 

Career opportunities for graduates include roles such as Planners, Designers, Constructors and Operators, Stewards of the Environment, Innovators and Integrators of Technology, Managers of Risk, and Leaders in Public Policy. Graduates can find opportunities in Public Sector Undertakings and the Government Sector. The scope for higher studies includes pursuing an M.E., M.Tech., or M.B.A.

## 3. Vision
The vision is to be a centre of excellence for transforming students into proficient Mechanical Engineers through sustainable practices.

## 4. Mission
The mission involves imparting core fundamental knowledge and necessary skills in Mechanical engineering through innovative teaching and learning methodologies. It aims to inculcate critical thinking, ethics, lifelong learning and creativity needed for industry and society. Furthermore, it cultivates the students with all-round competencies for their career, higher education and self employability.

## 5. Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs)
The Programme Educational Objectives state that graduates will be prepared for designing mechanical components and systems with creativity and sustainability. They will also be skilled in the use of modern tools for critical problem solving and analyzing industrial and societal requirements. In addition, graduates will be prepared with managerial and leadership skills for their career and for starting up their own firms.

## 6. Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
The Program Specific Outcomes emphasize that engineering graduates will be able to apply the acquired knowledge in mechanical engineering to solve industrial problems using modern tools. They will also develop cost effective and eco-friendly mechanical components and systems needed for the industry and society.

## 7. Programme Outcomes (PO)
The Programme Outcomes define the foundational abilities of the students. - **Programme Outcome (PO1) - Engineering Knowledge**: Engineering knowledge requires applying mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to solve complex engineering problems. - **Programme Outcome (PO2) - Problem Analysis**: Problem analysis involves identifying, formulating, reviewing research literature, and analyzing complex engineering problems to reach substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences. - **Programme Outcome (PO3) - Design/Development of Solutions**: For the design and development of solutions, students must design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, as well as cultural, societal, and environmental considerations. - **Programme Outcome (PO4) - Conduct Investigations**: Conducting investigations of complex problems requires using research-based knowledge and methods, including the design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of information to provide valid conclusions. - **Programme Outcome (PO5) - Modern Tool Usage**: Modern tool usage involves creating, selecting, and applying appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools, including prediction and modeling, to complex engineering activities with an understanding of their limitations.

- **Programme Outcome (PO6) - The Engineer and Society**: Further Programme Outcomes emphasize the engineer and society, applying reasoning informed by contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to professional engineering practice. - **Programme Outcome (PO7) - Environment and Sustainability**: Environment and sustainability focus on understanding the impact of professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, demonstrating the knowledge of and need for sustainable development. - **Programme Outcome (PO8) - Ethics**: Ethics involves applying ethical principles and committing to professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of engineering practice. - **Programme Outcome (PO9) - Individual and Team Work**: Individual and teamwork require functioning effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multidisciplinary settings. - **Programme Outcome (PO10) - Communication**: Communication ensures the ability to communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and society at large, including comprehending and writing effective reports, designing documentation, making effective presentations, and giving and receiving clear instructions. - **Programme Outcome (PO11) - Project Management and Finance**: Project management and finance involve demonstrating knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles and applying these to one's own work, managing projects, and working in multidisciplinary environments. - **Programme Outcome (PO12) - Life-long Learning**: Finally, life-long learning recognizes the need for and the ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

## 8. Job Profiles

### Employment Growth in Mechanical Engineering (2025–2030)
Job opportunities for mechanical engineers are widely available in India and abroad across both public and private sectors. There are numerous opportunities in automobiles, petroleum, oil and gas, transport, airport, aircraft, defense, railways, steel industries, power plants, and the major manufacturing sector. The employment growth for mechanical engineering in India by 2025 to 2030 is expected to be positive and growing, driven by multiple industry trends, technological advancements, and government initiatives.

### Key Drivers of Employment Growth
Industrial growth and infrastructure development are major drivers. Government initiatives like Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, and Smart Cities Mission will boost domestic manufacturing, construction, and infrastructure development. As India aims to become a global manufacturing hub, mechanical engineers will be needed for industries such as automotive, aerospace, energy, construction, and heavy machinery. Infrastructure projects such as high-speed rail, roads, bridges, and smart cities will drive demand for mechanical engineers in design, construction, and maintenance.

In the automotive industry, the transition to electric vehicles will accelerate the demand for mechanical engineers with expertise in electric powertrains, battery technology, and thermal management. For autonomous and connected vehicles, mechanical engineers will be involved in the design and manufacturing of advanced automotive systems, such as AI-based safety systems, autonomous driving technologies, and vehicle-to-everything communication. In renewable energy and sustainability, mechanical engineers will be involved in the design, installation, and maintenance of solar panels, wind turbines, and other green technologies. As industries seek to reduce energy consumption, mechanical engineers will play a critical role in designing energy-efficient systems and heat recovery systems.

Robotics and automation in manufacturing plants, warehouses, and service industries will drive demand for mechanical engineers who can design and integrate robotic systems, automated assembly lines, and precision equipment. Additive manufacturing will also require mechanical engineers with expertise in material science and CAD CAM systems. The Indian aerospace sector, with increasing investments in space exploration, aircraft manufacturing, and defense systems, will need mechanical engineers in areas such as propulsion systems, thermal management, and advanced materials. India's push for indigenous defense technology will require highly skilled mechanical engineers in defense manufacturing.

The integration of industrial internet of things with traditional manufacturing will drive the need for mechanical engineers who are well-versed in data analytics, sensor integration, and predictive maintenance. The adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies will promote the demand for engineers skilled in mechatronics and automation. Mechanical engineers will continue to be essential in the operation and maintenance of thermal power plants, nuclear energy plants, and gas turbines. With the rise in urbanization and demand for climate control, mechanical engineers will be needed for designing and maintaining heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems for large commercial buildings, hospitals, and smart homes.

Global trends such as offshoring and outsourcing are also creating opportunities, as global companies look to set up manufacturing plants in India due to competitive labor costs. Increased foreign direct investment and joint ventures with international companies in sectors like automotive and electronics will create global job prospects for Indian mechanical engineers.

### Employment Opportunities in High Demand
High demand roles include design engineers for product and process, manufacturing engineers, project managers for infrastructure, automotive, and heavy machinery, and robotics engineers. There are also high demands for automotive engineers focusing on electric vehicles and autonomous systems, energy systems engineers for renewables, HVAC, and power generation, and aerospace engineers. Maintenance engineers are needed for industrial plants, power plants, and HVAC systems. Other prominent roles include CAD CAE engineers, quality control and assurance engineers, R&D engineers for materials, robotics, and automotive, defense equipment engineers, and mechatronics engineers.

### Sectors with High Employment Potential
Sectors with high employment potential include the automotive and electric vehicle industry, renewable energy such as solar and wind, and the aerospace and defense sectors. There is also significant potential in construction and infrastructure, manufacturing and automation, robotics and mechatronics, and energy systems like thermal, gas, nuclear, and HVAC.

The curriculum includes subjects such as Engineering Graphics, Engineering Mechanics, Transforms and Partial Differential Equations, Engineering Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics and Machinery, Engineering Materials and Metallurgy, Manufacturing Processes, Theory of Machines, Thermal Engineering, Hydraulics and Pneumatics, Manufacturing Technology, Strength of Materials, Environmental Sciences and Sustainability, Design of Machine Elements, Metrology and Measurements, Non-Traditional Machining Process, Casting and Welding Process, Renewable Energy Technologies, and Disaster Risk Reduction and Management. # NAAC

## 1. NATIONAL ASSESSMENT AND ACCREDITATION COUNCIL (NAAC)

India boasts one of the largest and most diverse education systems globally, with significant advancements in recent years. The introduction of new and emerging programs, increased autonomy, and widespread expansion have collectively improved access to higher education. However, these developments have also raised concerns regarding the quality and relevance of higher education. In response to these concerns, the National Policy on Education (NPE) was introduced in 1986, followed by the Programme of Action (PoA) in 1992, which outlined strategic plans for addressing these issues and advocated for the establishment of an independent national accreditation agency.

Consequently, the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) was established in 1994 as an autonomous institution under the University Grants Commission (UGC), with its headquarters located in Bengaluru. The NAAC's vision statement reflects its core mandate, which is to integrate quality assurance into the functioning of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), thereby ensuring a commitment to excellence in education.

The National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) operates through two key bodies: the General Council (GC) and the Executive Committee (EC), both of which comprise a diverse group of educational administrators, policymakers, and senior academicians from various segments of the Indian higher education system.

At the helm of the NAAC's General Council is the Chairperson of the University Grants Commission (UGC), who serves as the President of the GC. The Chairperson of the Executive Committee, on the other hand, is an esteemed academician nominated by the President of the GC. This nomination process ensures that the EC is led by a highly respected and knowledgeable individual in the field of education.

The Director of the NAAC plays a pivotal role in the organization, serving as both the academic and administrative head. In addition to these responsibilities, the Director is also the member secretary of both the General Council and the Executive Committee, facilitating the smooth functioning of these bodies.

## 5. Best practices successfully implemented by **MSAJCE**

At Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering, **MSAJCE** has successfully implemented best practices to provide students with hands-on training through experiential learning, enabling them to obtain certification from reputable training agencies in cutting-edge technologies. 

The primary objective of this initiative is to equip students with multi-disciplinary skills, in addition to their core domain expertise, making them deployable in the job market. This is achieved through **MSAJCE**'s technology centres, which operate within regular college hours, allowing students to pursue training in areas of interest. 

To bridge the skill gap between students and employer expectations, **MSAJCE** has devised a structured training schedule that is prepared at the beginning of each academic year. These training sessions are conducted in the afternoon, without disrupting the regular academic schedule, and are led by certified faculty members who have obtained certification from various agencies. 

Students have the flexibility to choose courses that align with their interests, in addition to the scheduled training programs. Furthermore, the technology centres remain open beyond college working hours, allowing students to learn at their own pace. 

The success of this initiative is evident in the fact that students have obtained certification from renowned agencies such as CISCO, Altair, and Automation Anywhere. As a result, they have become not only employable but also directly deployable into jobs by recruited companies. Moreover, the hands-on experience gained through this training has equipped students with lifelong learning skills, enabling them to adapt to the ever-evolving job market.
